title: [Bug]: EngineCore hangs indefinitely in torch.xpu.graphs.replay() under concurrent load on Intel Arc B70 (Battlemage)
body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM version: 0.27.2rc1.dev77+gac7509e2b
torch: 2.13.0+xpu
GPU: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B70 Graphics (Battlemage), single device
Backend: native torch XPU (no IPEX installed)
Model: Qwen3-30B-A3B-class model, GPTQ Int4, served as "qwen38"
Launch flags (relevant):
  vllm serve /model --quantization gptq --dtype float16 \
    --max-model-len 110000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 9216 \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 --enable-log-requests
  (speculative decoding / MTP toggled via an env var wrapper around vllm serve;
   both MTP-on and MTP-off configurations reproduce this issue)
```

### Model Input Dumps

Not applicable — this is a hang, not a crash/incorrect-output bug, so there is no failing request payload to attach. Happy to capture one if it would help.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Under sustained concurrent load (2 agentic API clients issuing overlapping long-running
chat completions against the same server), the vLLM EngineCore process periodically
enters a genuine infinite spin inside `torch.xpu.graphs.replay()` (the CUDA/XPU-graph
replay call), pegging one CPU core at 100% and never returning. The server stops
responding to new requests; from the outside this looks like a hang, and our
`llama-swap`-based reverse proxy eventually kills and restarts the whole backend
service after its health probe (a real inference call) itself gets stuck behind the
spin.

This has recurred roughly every 10–25 minutes of concurrent-load runtime over
multiple independent sessions on this box, on both an MTP-enabled and an MTP-disabled
configuration, and is not correlated with `vllm:num_preemptions_total` (confirmed 0 at
the moment of at least one capture) or KV-cache eviction — i.e. it is not simply
"ran out of KV cache and got stuck recovering." It occurs while other engine threads
are otherwise idle (`Thread-1`/`Thread-2` housekeeping threads shown idle in every
capture below).

We confirmed this is a genuine spin, not a slow-but-progressing call, by taking
repeated `py-spy dump` snapshots of the same EngineCore PID several seconds apart:
the captured Python frame is byte-identical across snapshots, and `/proc/<pid>/stat`
cumulative CPU ticks climb steadily between snapshots (e.g. one PID: 55960 → 124899 →
263597 → 293561 ticks across four captures ~10–70 min apart, same top frame every time).

**Two distinct stack-trace variants of the same underlying `replay()` spin have been
observed** on this box, depending on whether speculative decoding (MTP) is enabled:

**Variant A — via the MTP/speculative-decode draft-proposal path:**
```
Thread (active): "MainThread"
    replay (torch/xpu/graphs.py:107)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360)
    execution_fn (<string>:10)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/caching.py:225)
    forward (vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py:284)
    __call__ (torch/_dynamo/aot_compile.py:244)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/decorators.py:520)
    propose (vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:755)
    propose_draft_token_ids (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:5366)
    propose_draft_token_ids (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:4718)
```

**Variant B — via the regular (non-speculative) decode forward path, observed after
disabling MTP as a mitigation attempt:**
```
Thread (active): "MainThread"
    replay (torch/xpu/graphs.py:107)
    __call__ (vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360)
    _model_forward (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:3970)
    execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:4554)
    decorate_context (torch/utils/_contextlib.py:124)
    execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:1086)
    decorate_context (torch/utils/_contextlib.py:124)
    execute_model (vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py:351)
    run_method (vllm/v1/serial_utils.py:510)
    collective_rpc (vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py:109)
```

Both bottom out at the identical frame: `replay (torch/xpu/graphs.py:107)` called from
`vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py:360`. This strongly suggests the bug is in the XPU
graph-replay call itself (or the state it depends on), not in either calling path —
MTP just changes which code path reaches it first/more often.

**Mitigation tried:** disabling MTP (speculative decoding) reduces frequency and
appears to make the spin less likely to require a full service restart to recover
from, and improves realized end-to-end throughput under concurrent load (measured
~44% higher tokens/sec over a wall-clock window, accounting for outage time), but does
**not** eliminate the spin — Variant B above was captured with MTP fully disabled.

**Independent third-party corroboration:** a public benchmarking log for the same
GPU (`steveseguin/b70-optimization-lab`, README) documents XPU-graph + MTP
producing corrupted/zero-acceptance output on this hardware generation:
> `MTP1 + XPU graph | 7.63 tok/s | 0.00 acceptance | corrupt (0/25) - do not use`
> `MTP off, XPU graph on (two boots) | 30.22 / 30.26 tok/s | - | faithful (23/25, within boot envelope)`

That log documents output corruption specifically with MTP+graph, which is a
different symptom (wrong output vs. our hang) but points at the same suspect
component (XPU graph replay interacting with speculative decoding) on the same GPU
family, and independently supports MTP+graph being unreliable on Battlemage.

Related-but-not-identical issues we found and ruled out as duplicates:
- vllm-project/vllm#48327 — same class of Intel-XPU CUDA-graph-replay issue, but
  reported as producing garbage output, not a hang.
- pytorch/pytorch#187277 — XPU graph replay crash (not a spin) on similar hardware.

Neither exactly matches a genuine infinite spin with climbing CPU and no crash/error,
so filing this as a distinct report rather than a duplicate.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve a GPTQ-quantized model on a single Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage) via vLLM's
   native XPU backend, with CUDA/XPU graph capture enabled (default), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
2. Drive sustained concurrent load: 2+ long-running agentic/chat-completion clients
   issuing overlapping requests continuously for tens of minutes.
3. Periodically (observed every ~10–25 min of concurrent runtime), the EngineCore
   process's MainThread enters `torch.xpu.graphs.replay()` and never returns; CPU
   usage for that thread pegs at 100% indefinitely. Confirm via repeated `py-spy dump`
   of the EngineCore PID showing an identical frame with climbing `/proc/<pid>/stat`
   CPU ticks across snapshots taken minutes apart.
4. The server stops answering any new request; recovery currently requires a full
   process restart (nothing short of restart has been found to un-stick it).

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [ROCm] AITER v0.1.23 bump: gfx950 a16w4 MXFP4 MoE Gluon backend crashes (AttributeError get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout)
body:
## Report of bug

Bumping AITER to v0.1.23 (#58867) surfaced two upstream regressions, one already fixed in that PR and one filed upstream for tracking.

### 1. `upcast_from_mxfp` removed from `aiter.ops.triton.moe.quant_moe` (fixed)

ROCm/aiter#5259 removed the public `upcast_from_mxfp` helper with no replacement shipped in the pip package. Only used by `tests/kernels/moe/test_ocp_mx_moe.py`, which had its own equivalent pure-PyTorch `mxfp4_dequantize` helper already — fixed by reusing that instead of the aiter import (already included in #58867).

### 2. gfx950 `moe_gemm_a16w4` Gluon backend crash (production-path regression)

ROCm/aiter#5355 (in v0.1.23) added a Gluon-based `moe_gemm_a16w4` kernel for gfx950 and widened `_GLUON_SUPPORTED_ARCHS` to include it, so the default (`backend=None`) auto-detect on gfx950 now always routes to Gluon. That kernel calls `gl.amd.get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout(...)`, a Triton-Gluon AMD API only added upstream in triton-lang/triton#11470 (merged 2026-09-08) — newer than the Triton commit vLLM's ROCm images currently pin (`669b31a`, 2026-08-28) — causing:

```
AttributeError("module 'triton.experimental.gluon.language.amd' has no attribute 'get_scaled_upcast_fp4_scale_layout'")
```

This hits `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/aiter_mxfp4_w4a16_moe.py`, i.e. any gfx950 (MI355) model using AITER's a16w4 MXFP4 MoE path (e.g. gpt-oss), not just tests.

Filed upstream: ROCm/aiter#5888.

**Workaround applied in #58867**: pass `backend="triton"` explicitly on gfx950 for both `moe_gemm_a16w4()` calls, forcing the known-good path until aiter guards its Gluon auto-detect against this Triton version gap (or vLLM's pinned Triton is updated past triton-lang/triton#11470).

### Confirmation

Filing this mainly for tracking/visibility — the fix is already in #58867. Will close once that PR merges, or if the aiter-side fix (ROCm/aiter#5888) lands and we want to revert the workaround.

### Before submitting a new issue

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the vLLM community for help

title: [Bug]: Engine startup on DGX Spark (GB10, unified memory) collapses host memory — NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY while MemAvailable reports ~22 GiB
body:
### Your current environment

- **Hardware:** NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10, SM121, aarch64, **121.7 GiB unified memory**, driver **580.173.02**, CUDA 13.0, kernel **7.0.0-1019-nvidia**
- **vLLM:** 0.29.0 (torch 2.13.0+cu130)
- **Model:** `RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` (Qwen4Exp architecture), `--tensor-parallel-size 1`
- **Flags:** `--quantization modelopt`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.70`, MTP k=3 via `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`, `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[4,8,12,16,20,24]}'`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--no-enable-prefix-caching`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`
- **Important:** **no request is served.** This happens during engine initialization only, at the KV-cache / graph-capture phase, right after `Loading weights took 549.60 seconds` and the encoder-cache initialization.

### Describe the bug

The engine drives the unified memory pool to exhaustion during startup and the driver reports failure while the host still reports plenty of free memory. Host memory collapses within seconds (sampled every 2 s):

| ts | MemAvailable | physical used | cgroup `memory.current` | residual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13:23:44 | 29.083 | 92.605 | 23.581 | 82.050 |
| 13:23:46 | 29.081 | 92.607 | 23.581 | 82.053 |
| 13:23:48 | 29.079 | 92.609 | 23.582 | 82.055 |
| 13:23:50 | 29.077 | 92.611 | 23.581 | 82.057 |
| 13:23:52 | 25.931 | 95.757 | 25.999 | 82.653 |
| 13:23:55 | 20.180 | 101.508 | 31.671 | 80.722 |
| 13:23:57 | 11.469 | 110.219 | 33.197 | 80.859 |
| 13:23:59 | **2.538** | **119.150** | 33.972 | 81.343 |

(values in GiB; `physical used = MemTotal - MemAvailable`; `residual = MemTotal - MemFree - Active - Inactive - Slab - PageTables - Unevictable`)

**29 GiB disappeared in 9 seconds.** At the same time the driver logged:

```
NVRM: nvCheckOkFailedNoLog: Check failed: Out of memory [NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY] (0x00000051) returned from _memdescAllocInternal(pMemDesc) @ mem_desc.c:1359
```

### Why the host cannot see it

- physical peak **119.2 / 121.7 GiB**, while the engine's process RSS was **1.8 GiB** and its cgroup `memory.current` never exceeded **34 GiB**
- not page cache: `Cached` was 19.8 GiB and is fully accounted for
- on the same host at idle the residual is **1.1 GiB**; under load it is **77-90 GiB**
- `MemAvailable` reported **22.5 GiB free at the moment the driver failed**

Consequence for operators: no host-side signal (meminfo, PSI, vmstat) can trigger a guard before the device allocation is already failing.

### Workaround

Reducing the startup allocation footprint keeps the host healthy (same host, same model, same flags otherwise):

| config | min MemAvailable | max physical | max cgroup `memory.current` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--max-num-seqs 256`, `--max-model-len 32768` | **2.54 GiB** | 119.2 GiB | 34 GiB |
| `--max-num-seqs 32`, `--max-model-len 16384` | **22.5 GiB** | 99.2 GiB | 16.7 GiB |

Note: `NV_ERR_NO_MEMORY` still appears with the reduced configuration, so that message alone is not a reliable indicator — it looks like a retry pattern. The reliable signal is the host-side residual.

An external 2-second host guard (stop the unit below a hard `MemAvailable` line) is what kept this box out of a kernel OOM: 0 `oom-kill` events across all runs, while a comparable earlier configuration produced 197 kernel OOM dumps over two days.

### Hypothesis

Same class as #56457 / #55569: allocations streamed through the caching allocator whose size grows monotonically. On a discrete GPU `cudaMalloc` eventually fails and the allocator flushes its cache and retries; on unified-memory GB10 `cudaMalloc` keeps succeeding until the driver has nothing left, so the failure surfaces as a device-allocation error (and a host-memory collapse) instead of a Python OOM. Here the source is the startup KV-cache profiling / graph capture rather than a long prefill.

The fix direction from those issues (reusable or coarse-rounded buckets / workspace manager) would address this case as well.

### Disclosure

Local overlays are applied to this build: PLE disk-offload (model weights partially NVMe-backed), an MTP index remap, and a one-line `modelopt.py` dispatch fix. `models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ops/qsa_indexer.py` is **unmodified** upstream — we verified it uses the fixed page-table width (`columns = page_table.shape[1] * k_cache.shape[1]`) and therefore does **not** carry the #56457 regression. The startup curve is therefore partially build-specific; the invisibility mechanism is not.

Full 2-second telemetry (all runs, TSV) and the sampling script are available on request.

---
*Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed and validated end-to-end by Stefan Kaiser ([@kaiste99](https://github.com/kaiste99)).*

title: [Performance]: GLM-5.3-Flash on H100: auto-selected FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 is 36-70% slower than FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>vllm collect-env (abridged)</summary>

```
OS                           : Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
PyTorch version              : 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA runtime version         : 13.0.88
GPU                          : 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (single node, TP=8)
Nvidia driver version        : 595.71.05
vLLM Version                 : 0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b (git sha: 385dce36b)
Docker image                 : vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash @ sha256:819ec9c063412e5730d1b0e82046ba540d1bf991f3c4f661a849aae8a0c52374
[pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.18
[pip3] torch==2.13.0+cu130
[pip3] triton==3.7.1
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Summary:** For `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on H100 the auto-selected sparse-MLA attention backend is `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (log: `Using FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90', 'FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE']`). It is **~36% slower at concurrency 1 and ~70% slower at concurrency 8** than the other candidate, `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE`, measured with `vllm bench serve` on the same server flags. MTP draft acceptance is identical across the two, so the gap is per-step attention cost, not speculative-decoding behaviour. Forcing `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` recovers it.

**How we found it:** we had been serving from an image built on 2026-08-26 from the `glm-release` branch (base `487ecf187`, FlashInfer 0.6.17). That build logs `Using FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE', 'FLASHMLA_SPARSE']`. After moving to the current `vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash` (nightly `385dce36b`, FlashInfer 0.6.18) with identical flags, the backend line changed to `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` and single-stream throughput dropped by roughly a third. The preference appears to come from #53906 (`031c899d` "[Model] Use FlashInfer for GLM-5.3-Flash NoPE MLA", `e34f7f71` "[Kernel] Use FlashInfer rc10 for NoPE MLA") and is gated on the FlashInfer version, so the 0.6.17 -> 0.6.18 bump flipped the kernel without any flag change.

**Server launch (both runs identical except the one flag):**

```bash
docker run --gpus all --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
  -v /path/to/hf-cache:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  -e VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
  vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash \
  zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}' \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 512
  # "FA3" rows add:  --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE
```

**Benchmark (run inside the same container):**

```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --model zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --dataset-name sonnet --dataset-path /vllm-workspace/benchmarks/sonnet.txt \
  --sonnet-input-len 300 --sonnet-output-len 256 --sonnet-prefix-len 100 \
  --num-prompts 20 --num-warmups 2 --max-concurrency {1,8} --ignore-eos --disable-shuffle --temperature 0 --seed 0
# "random" rows: --dataset-name random --random-input-len 300 --random-output-len 256
```

| dataset | max-concurrency | backend | output tok/s | mean TPOT | mean ITL | median E2E (256 tok) | MTP accept len / rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sonnet | 1 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **368.8** | 2.28 ms | 10.9 ms | 698 ms | 4.89 / 77.8% |
| sonnet | 1 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 237.0 | 3.83 ms | 18.3 ms | 1064 ms | 4.89 / 77.7% |
| sonnet | 8 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **754.1** | 5.00 ms | 23.9 ms | 1914 ms | 4.90 / 77.9% |
| sonnet | 8 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 229.8 | 17.4 ms | 82.9 ms | 5470 ms | 4.87 / 77.3% |
| random | 1 | `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` (forced) | **249.3** | 3.59 ms | 10.9 ms | 1006 ms | 3.08 / 41.7% |
| random | 1 | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` (default) | 162.9 | 5.78 ms | 17.0 ms | 1570 ms | 2.97 / 39.5% |

(sonnet is a best case for MTP on this model, random a worst case; the ratio between backends is the same in both.) Same picture with `--enable-expert-parallel` (recipe TEP strategy) and with the Hopper recipe override `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`.

**Expected:** the auto-selected backend should not be materially slower than an available alternative on the same hardware; or the recipe should document `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` for Hopper.

**Related:** forcing `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE` on this nightly floods the log with `Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 1` from zero-extent descriptors (outputs correct; 0 such messages with the default backend). Filed separately: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56563.

body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

I started hacking on vLLM recently for RamaLama and other reasons to see what the hardware support is like compared to llama.cpp. The one big noticeable gap is Vulkan support. It would solve a bunch of problems around vLLM not running great on commodity hardware:

https://github.com/containers/ramalama/pull/1677

### Alternatives

Use llama.cpp

### Additional context

_No response_

title: [Hybrid GDN] Explicit --block-size misaligned with mamba page makes SimpleCPU KV offload silently write-only; startup should reject or warn
body:
# Upstream issue draft（送 admin 过目版 v1，2026-09-24；联合署名 llm-1 & f280，admin 09-23 23:47Z 批）

> 投 vLLM GitHub issue 前的内部草稿。证据双方独立实测，可逐条复算。

---

**Title**: `[Hybrid GDN] Explicit --block-size misaligned with mamba page makes SimpleCPU KV offload silently write-only; startup should reject or warn`

## Summary

On hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 family, `linear_attention` + periodic `full_attention`), enabling the SimpleCPU KV offload connector (`VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`) together with an **explicit** `--block-size` that does not match the mamba-page alignment results in the offload connector becoming **write-only**: blocks are stored to CPU (RSS grows, write path active) but the read path never serves a single token (`external_kv_transfer` stays 0, re-prefill after forced eviction costs the same as a cold prefill). Omitting `--block-size` (letting the engine auto-compute the aligned size) makes the same setup fully functional. The failure is **silent** — no error, no warning — and looks exactly like "offload enabled" from the outside.

## Environment (two independent deployments, same wheel)

- vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev400+g38537331d`; model Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (AutoRound / AWQ-INT4), `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid GDN: 48 GDN `linear_attention` + 16 `full_attention` (interval=4), mamba align, 1 MTP layer
- **Deployment A (llm-1)**: fp8 KV, MTP on, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.93`, `--kv-offloading-size 16` (GiB), mamba cache fp16
- **Deployment B (f280)**: fp8 KV, MTP on, `--kv-cache-memory 8105442816` (pool 208,005 tok), CPU offload 30 GB / 584 blocks, mamba cache fp32
- Both: `VLLM_USE_SIMPLE_KV_OFFLOAD=1`, prefix caching on, `max_model_len=131072`

> Note on version: filed against a dev build (`0.29.1rc1.dev400`) because both deployments run it in production; the same checks have **not** yet been run on a stable release. If the stable branch behaves differently we will report back.

## Symptom (deployment A, explicit `--block-size 128`)

- Startup log: `Setting attention block size to 896 tokens to ensure that attention page size is >= mamba page size` → `kv cache group sizes [896, 896, 896, 896]`
- Write path alive: connector RSS grows ~16 GiB under eviction pressure (all FA blocks)
- Read path dead: probe = T1 cold prefill of a 30k-token doc, T2 warm re-ask (local hit), force eviction with 6×35k-token filler docs, 75 s drain, T3 re-ask:
  - **T3/T1 = 1.006–1.46** (re-ask after eviction ≈ full cold prefill)
  - **Δ`prompt_tokens_by_source{external_kv_transfer}` = 0** across the T3 window
- No error/warning anywhere in logs.

## Fix-by-configuration (both deployments, read path fully functional)

Dropping the explicit flag → engine auto-computes the aligned block size:

| Deployment | Startup fingerprint | T3/T1 | Δ external_kv_transfer (T3 window) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, `--block-size 128` | `[896×4]` | 1.006–1.46 | **0** |
| A, flag omitted | `Setting attention block size to 816` / `[816×4]` | **0.032 / 0.048** (two windows) | **+29,376** |
| B, flag omitted (fp32 mamba) | `Setting attention block size to 1584` / `[1584×4]` | **0.044** (re-run 0.0438; instrumented variant 0.1279) | **+28,512** |

Answers identical across T1/T2/T3 in all runs. The only changed variable between the broken and working rows on deployment A is the explicit `--block-size` flag (single-variable matrix over {mamba dtype, async_scheduling, cumem, block-size} — block-size was the only HIT).

## Expected behavior

When a hybrid-GDN model is configured with an explicit `--block-size` whose resulting attention page geometry is incompatible with the mamba page / offload connector granularity, vLLM should **refuse to start or at least emit a loud WARN**, instead of running silently with a write-only offload connector.

Suggested improvements (joint appendix):
1. **Startup validation**: reject or WARN when explicit `--block-size` conflicts with mamba-page alignment for hybrid models (the auto-align path `interface.py:918` already computes the correct value — the explicit-flag path appears to bypass the same protection, raising to a value (896) that satisfies the page-size inequality but breaks connector store/load granularity).
2. **Connector robustness**: SimpleCPU connector should detect the granularity mismatch and fail loudly rather than store-never-load.
3. **Observability**: expose store/load counter pairs in `/metrics` so "write-only offload" is directly visible (today only `external_kv_transfer` hits/queries tell the story indirectly).

## Notes

- Without KV offloading, the explicit `--block-size 128` is harmless: it is raised to 896 and never actually runs at 128 — inference correctness is unaffected. The bug only bites the offload read path.
- Reproduction probe and full datasets available on request (both deployments, archived JSON + logs).

*Joint report by the maintainers of two independent production deployments (anonymous), independent reproductions on an identical wheel build, 2026-09-24.*

title: [Bug]: Intermittent Xid 31 MMU fault in pynccl all_reduce during CUDA graph
body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.29.0 (image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0 + ray 2.56.1, pip package b12x 1.3.0)
torch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, transformers 5.16.1
GPU: 6x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), driver 595.91.07
Host: Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic, Docker
Cluster: two nodes (4 + 2 GPUs), Ray 2.56.1, 100 GbE direct link
Model: nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4, PP=3 / TP=2, VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=31,29,18

Launch command:

  vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --distributed-executor-backend ray \
    --pipeline-parallel-size 3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"b12x","linear_backend":"flashinfer_b12x",
                      "enable_cutedsl_warmup":true,"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \
    --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa":true}' \
    --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-async-scheduling \
    --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.98

Note: --disable-custom-all-reduce is required on SM120, so every reduction goes
through the pynccl path.

(collect_env.py output can be provided on request - the engine runs inside a
container on a two-node Ray cluster, so the script does not capture the full
picture.)


### 🐛 Describe the bug

Roughly every third engine start dies during CUDA graph capture. The crash is a
driver-level Xid 31 MMU fault; on the Python side it surfaces as an NCCL error
inside the tensor-parallel all_reduce that is being captured. It is intermittent:
the identical command succeeds on the next attempt, and once the engine is up it
serves for days without a single Xid.

Kernel log:

    NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:41:00): 31, pid=147307, name=ray::vllm_Worke,
    channel 0x00000002, intr 00000000. MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC0
    GPCCLIENT_T1_0 faulted @ 0x284_e8006000.
    Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ

Engine log - the crash happens at "Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL): 71%|5/7",
in Worker_PP1_TP0:

    reduced = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(hidden_states)
      -> get_tp_group().all_reduce(input_)
      -> torch.ops.vllm.all_reduce(input_, group_name=...)
      -> group._all_reduce_out_place(tensor)
      -> self.device_communicator.all_reduce(input_)
      -> out = pynccl_comm.all_reduce(input_)
      -> self.nccl.ncclAllReduce(...)
      -> RuntimeError: NCCL error: unhandled cuda error
    During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
      torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

## Controlled comparison

Same hardware, same command, only --enforce-eager added. All other models shut
down, GPUs verified free between runs:

    with graph capture   first-attempt failures ~30 % (6 of 22)   startup ~3:00 min
    --enforce-eager      first-attempt failures 0 of 8            startup ~1:45 min

22 first attempts recorded over five days; 6 died this way. Two further failures
were an unrelated out-of-memory condition and are excluded. In a deliberate
reproduction run today the failure appeared on the 4th consecutive start.

Seven Xid occurrences so far, on all four GPUs of the head node (PCI 01:00,
21:00, 41:00, 61:00), so this is not a defective card. The faulting addresses
repeat across incidents (0x284_e8006000 four times, 0x24f_78006000 twice).

## What we ruled out

- GPU memory pressure: same behaviour at --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 and 0.98.
  At crash time the cards sit at 95.8 GiB of 97.9 GiB, 350 W power cap, 33 C.
- Defective hardware: all four GPUs of the head node produced the fault.
- #50189: that is a *write* fault under concurrent load with the flashinfer_b12x
  MoE backend. We use the native b12x MoE backend, our fault is a *read* at
  startup, and the engine never faults while serving.
- #40742: requires PDL (we set neither TRTLLM_ENABLE_PDL nor
  TORCHINDUCTOR_ENABLE_PDL) and raises "operation not permitted when stream is
  capturing", not a driver Xid.
- #30044: GH200, no Xid, deterministic rather than intermittent.

## Guess at the mechanism

Capturing an ncclAllReduce inside a CUDA graph appears to hit a race. The
faulting addresses repeat across incidents, which looks more like a deterministic
allocation being touched at the wrong moment than random corruption. We cannot
verify this from the outside.

## Workaround

Our autostart script retries up to five times, waiting for all GPUs to be
released between attempts; attempt 1 or 2 normally succeeds. --enforce-eager
avoids the fault entirely at the cost of throughput.

Full engine log, dmesg excerpt and nvidia-smi output of a failing run are saved
and can be attached on request.

title: [Bug]:  GLM-5.3-MXFP4 DP8 without EP crashes during FlashInfer autotune with CUDA illegal memory access
body:
### Your current environment


Hardware: 8× NVIDIA GB300  
vLLM commit: `4be061c5afab`  
PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description

GLM-5.3-MXFP4 fails to start with TP1/DP8 and expert parallelism disabled. The crash occurs during the 32K-token FlashInfer autotune dummy run in sparse MLA logical-to-physical top-k index conversion.

This reproduces on a clean vLLM `main` build and is unrelated to our CUTLASS MXFP4 EP changes.

### Reproduction

Hardware: 8× NVIDIA B300  
vLLM commit: `4be061c5afab`  
PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
VLLM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_EXPERT_FP4_MOE=262144 \
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser glm47 \
  --data-parallel-size 8 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --block-size 64 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching
Do not pass --enable-expert-parallel.
Error
All eight DP workers fail after:
Running FlashInfer autotune with 32768 tokens
The relevant stack is:
flashinfer_mla_sparse.py::forward_mqa
sparse_mla_attention.py::_convert_logical_to_physical_topk
index_group.py::_convert_once
sparse_utils.py::triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index

RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
Additional information
Without VLLM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_EXPERT_FP4_MOE=262144, startup fails earlier because DP8 all-gather produces m_numtopk=2097152, exceeding the default MXFP4 capacity.
PR #56825 is already present in this commit. That PR fixes a piecewise CUDA graph event error, while this failure occurs in the workspace-overflow conversion path during FlashInfer autotune.
```

title: [Bug][ROCm]: GPU memory fault in AITER MLA FP8 prefill under async scheduling (race on persistent PS metadata)
body:
**Fix:** #58887 plans the FP8 prefill metadata into pinned host staging and copies it on the current stream, so the update is ordered after in-flight prefill kernels. AITER-side follow-up: [ROCm/aiter#5879](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5879). ## Your current environment | | | | --- | --- | | Image | `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098` | | vLLM | `0.30.1rc1.dev143+g29468dde8` | | ROCm / HIP | ROCm 10 (HIP 7.15), torch `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, triton `3.8.0` | | AITER | `amd-aiter 0.1.22.post1` | | GPU | 8x MI355X (gfx950) | | Model | `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`, TP8 (12 attention heads per rank, padded to 16 for AITER) | The ROCm 7.2 image of the same nightly (`nightly-29468dde…`, ROCm 7.2.3, triton 3.7.1) did not fault on the same end-to-end workload, but it has the same race: the standalone reproduction below faults on both runtimes. In serving, the 7.2 plan copy happens to wait behind work already queued on the GPU (see "Why ROCm 7.2 does not show it end to end"). The Python code and the AITER ASM kernels are byte-identical between the two images. ## 🐛 Describe the bug With `ROCM_AITER_MLA`, an FP8 KV cache and async scheduling, serving crashes with a GPU memory fault while under load. The FP8 MLA prefill path (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) reads its scheduling metadata from one set of persistent device buffers. Those buffers are rewritten for every batch that contains a new prefill, by host code that is not ordered on the current stream. With async scheduling, the rewrite for step N+1 can land while step N's prefill kernels are still queued. Step N then runs with step N+1's work/reduce maps. ### Minimal reproduction Dummy weights are enough. ```bash docker run --rm --entrypoint '' --network host --ipc host \ --device /dev/kfd --device /dev/dri --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --shm-size 128G \ -v $HF_HOME/hub:/root/.cache/huggingface/hub \ -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MLA=1 \ -e VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 -e VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 \ -e VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \ vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098 \ vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --load-format dummy --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --async-scheduling --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' ``` ```bash python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random \ --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --port 8000 --request-rate inf \ --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 \ --max-concurrency 32 --num-prompts 1024 --warmup-requests 32 --seed 4 ``` On a given machine the fault is deterministic for a given request stream (same request count every run). Whether a given stream triggers it varies, so try a few: | Stream (8k/1k) | Fault at request | | --- | --- | | concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 4 | 111 (x3; also with `--enforce-eager`) | | concurrency 32, 2048 prompts | 79 | | concurrency 64, 1024 prompts | 61 | | concurrency 32, 1024 prompts, seed 5 | 117 | 128 prompts is usually too little exposure. Each fault shows up in under 10 minutes including server startup. ### Also reproduces with DeepSeek-V3 Same image and server flags, with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3` (TP8, 128 heads, 16 per rank, so no head padding) instead of Kimi-K3 and without the Kimi-K3-specific parser options, dummy weights, same benchmark command: | Stream (8k/1k, concurrency 32, 1024 prompts) | Unpatched | With the proposed fix | | --- | --- | --- | | seed 4 | fault at request 111 | 1024/1024 | | seed 5 | fault at request 117 | not run | The engine dump at the fault shows the same crash batch: one new 8175-token prefill with 32 running requests. So the race is in the shared FP8 MLA prefill path, not in anything specific to Kimi-K3. ### Standalone reproduction (no server, one gfx950 GPU) The same race, isolated with the same AITER calls vLLM makes. It reproduces on ROCm 7.2 as well as ROCm 10: 1. Plan batch A (one 8175-token prefill, no partial tiles) into persistent device buffers with `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1`. 2. On a non-blocking `torch.cuda.Stream()` (the stream vLLM uses), queue a GPU delay (`torch.cuda._sleep`), then A's `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`. 3. Immediately plan batch B (three prefills: 6992, 6896, 2495 tokens) into the same buffers from the host, as step N+1's metadata build does under async scheduling. 4. Synchronize and compare A's output with a reference run. | Mode | ROCm 7.2 | ROCm 10 | | --- | --- | --- | | as above (vLLM's current pattern) | GPU memory fault on the first iteration | GPU memory fault on the first iteration | | `stream.synchronize()` before planning B | output matches reference | output matches reference | | plan B into pinned host memory, `copy_(non_blocking=True)` on the stream (proposed fix) | output matches reference | output matches reference | The fault has the serving signature: `Memory access fault ... on address 0x1d000` / `0x64000`, `Write access to a read-only page` (or `Unknown`). Script: `aiter_ps_metadata_race.py` ([gist](https://gist.github.com/amd-mghanimi/970e190ceea417467594980b96f3604b), also inlined below). Run it inside either vLLM ROCm image with `python3 aiter_ps_metadata_race.py`. Add `--streams 12` for the per-stream table in "Why ROCm 7.2 does not show it end to end".
aiter_ps_metadata_race.py (standalone reproducer) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Standalone reproducer: AITER MLA FP8 prefill plan rewritten while in use (vLLM async scheduling). Mirrors vLLM's ROCM_AITER_MLA FP8 prefill (rocm_aiter_mla.py @ 29468dde, _build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata + _mla_fp8_prefill_attn) on one gfx950 GPU: 1. Plan batch A (one 8175-token prefill) into persistent device buffers with aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1, as vLLM does. 2. On a non-blocking stream (as vLLM uses), queue a GPU delay standing in for step N's earlier layers, then A's mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd + mla_reduce_v1. 3. Immediately plan batch B (three prefills) into the same buffers from the host, as step N+1's metadata build does under async scheduling. 4. Synchronize and compare A's output with a reference. Default run, one stream, three modes (each in its own process, since a GPU fault kills it): race vLLM's current pattern: device outputs, stream-less hipMemcpy inside AITER. synced stream.synchronize() before planning B. fixed plan into pinned host staging, copy_(non_blocking=True) on the stream (the vLLM fix). python3 aiter_ps_metadata_race.py Expected on ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10 alike: race faults, synced and fixed match the reference. Why ROCm 7.2 serving can still look fine: python3 aiter_ps_metadata_race.py --streams 12 runs the race on each of 12 non-blocking streams. It first probes which streams a stream-less 1 KiB hipMemcpy waits behind, i.e. which share the null stream's in-order hardware queue. AITER's first plan copy is that small, so it runs as a copy kernel on the null stream's queue. Only prefill streams on a shared queue are protected. Queue assignment differs between ROCm versions and runtime settings (try DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=1 or GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16 on ROCm 7.2). """ import argparse import ctypes import json import os import subprocess import sys import time TILE_Q = 256 # _FP8_PREFILL_TILE_Q NHEAD = 16 # 12 heads/rank (Kimi-K3 TP8) replicate-padded to 16 for the ASM prefill QK_DIM, V_DIM = 192, 128 # mla_pfl_qh192_vh128_* MAX_REQS, MAX_TOKENS = 256, 16384 BATCH_A = [8175] # the crash batch's prefill BATCH_B = [6992, 6896, 2495] # a following multi-prefill batch PLAN_KW = dict(qhead_granularity=1, qlen_granularity=TILE_Q, kvlen_granularity=128, block_size=1, is_causal=True) def alloc_plan_buffers(torch, device, pin=False): from aiter import get_ps_metadata_info_v1 info = get_ps_metadata_info_v1(batch_size=MAX_REQS, num_head_k=NHEAD, max_qlen=MAX_TOKENS, qlen_granularity=TILE_Q) bufs = [] for size, dtype in info: shape = size if isinstance(size, tuple) else (size,) bufs.append(torch.empty(*shape, dtype=dtype, device=device, pin_memory=pin and device == "cpu")) return bufs # work_meta, work_indptr, work_info, reduce_indptr, reduce_final, reduce_partial def plan(torch, bufs, seq_lens): from aiter import get_ps_metadata_v1 lens = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32) qo = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens) + 1, dtype=torch.int32) qo[1:] = lens.cumsum(0) get_ps_metadata_v1(qo, qo.clone(), lens, 1, NHEAD, *bufs, **PLAN_KW) class PrefillA: def __init__(self, torch): self.torch = torch torch.manual_seed(0) total = sum(BATCH_A) fp8 = torch.float8_e4m3fn self.q = (torch.randn(total, NHEAD, QK_DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(fp8) self.k = (torch.randn(total, NHEAD, QK_DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(fp8) self.v = (torch.randn(total, NHEAD, V_DIM, device="cuda") * 0.5).to(fp8) self.qo = torch.tensor([0, total], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") self.kv_indices = torch.arange(total, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") self.total = total self.one = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda") # vLLM carves per-call scratch from a pre-reserved workspace. self.workspace = torch.empty(64 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") def launch(self, dev_bufs, num_partial_tiles): from aiter import mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd, mla_reduce_v1 torch = self.torch shapes = [((num_partial_tiles * TILE_Q, NHEAD, V_DIM), torch.float32), ((num_partial_tiles * TILE_Q, NHEAD), torch.float32), ((self.total, NHEAD), torch.float32)] scratch, off = [], 0 for s, d in shapes: n = torch.Size(s).numel() * torch.empty((), dtype=d).element_size() scratch.append(self.workspace[off:off + n].view(d).view(s)) off += (n + 255) // 256 * 256 logits, lse, final_lse = scratch _, work_indptr, work_info, reduce_indptr, reduce_final, reduce_partial = dev_bufs out = torch.empty(self.total, NHEAD, V_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda") mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd(self.q, self.k, self.v, self.qo, self.qo, self.kv_indices, work_indptr, work_info, max(BATCH_A), QK_DIM ** -0.5, True, logits, lse, out, self.one, self.one, self.one) mla_reduce_v1(logits, lse, reduce_indptr, reduce_final, reduce_partial, TILE_Q, 0, out, final_lse) return out def child(mode, num_streams, index, iters, delay_ms, probe): import numpy as np import torch print(f"HIPVER {torch.version.hip}", flush=True) torch.zeros(1, device="cuda") # the null stream exists first, as in frameworks # Load AITER and allocate before creating streams, as vLLM does (model load, then streams). dev_bufs = alloc_plan_buffers(torch, "cuda") staging = [alloc_plan_buffers(torch, "cpu", pin=True) for _ in range(2)] a = PrefillA(torch) plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_A) torch.cuda.synchronize() streams = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(num_streams)] # HIP binds a stream to a hardware queue at its first launch; launch on every stream once, # in order, so the stream-to-queue mapping does not depend on the tested index. for s in streams: with torch.cuda.stream(s): torch.cuda._sleep(1000) torch.cuda.synchronize() stream = streams[index] with torch.cuda.stream(stream): torch.cuda._sleep(1_000_000) t0, t1 = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True) t0.record() torch.cuda._sleep(50_000_000) t1.record() t1.synchronize() cycles = int(50_000_000 * delay_ms / t0.elapsed_time(t1)) if probe: hip = ctypes.CDLL("libamdhip64.so") hip.hipMemcpy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_int] dst = torch.empty(1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda") src = np.zeros(1024, dtype=np.uint8) hip.hipMemcpy(dst.data_ptr(), src.ctypes.data, 1024, 1) torch.cuda.synchronize() shared = [] for j, s in enumerate(streams): with torch.cuda.stream(s): torch.cuda._sleep(cycles) t = time.perf_counter() hip.hipMemcpy(dst.data_ptr(), src.ctypes.data, 1024, 1) if (time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000.0 > 0.5 * delay_ms: shared.append(j) torch.cuda.synchronize() print("PROBE " + json.dumps(shared), flush=True) with torch.cuda.stream(stream): plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_A) ref = a.launch(dev_bufs, int(dev_bufs[3][-1].item())) torch.cuda.synchronize() mismatches, walls = 0, [] for it in range(iters): with torch.cuda.stream(stream): if mode == "fixed": host = staging[it % 2] plan(torch, host, BATCH_A) for d, h in zip(dev_bufs[1:], host[1:]): d.copy_(h, non_blocking=True) tiles = int(host[3][-1]) else: plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_A) tiles = int(dev_bufs[3][-1].item()) torch.cuda._sleep(cycles) # step N's earlier layers still running out = a.launch(dev_bufs, tiles) # step N's prefill reads the plan if mode == "synced": stream.synchronize() t = time.perf_counter() if mode == "fixed": # step N+1's plan, stream-ordered host = staging[(it + 1) % 2] plan(torch, host, BATCH_B) for d, h in zip(dev_bufs[1:], host[1:]): d.copy_(h, non_blocking=True) else: # step N+1's plan, stream-less hipMemcpy into the shared buffers plan(torch, dev_bufs, BATCH_B) walls.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000.0) torch.cuda.synchronize() mismatches += int((out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item() > 0) print("RESULT " + json.dumps({"mismatches": mismatches, "plan_b_ms": round(sum(walls) / len(walls), 1)}), flush=True) def run_child(args, mode, num_streams, index, probe): cmd = [sys.executable, os.path.abspath(__file__), "--child", mode, "--streams", str(num_streams), "--index", str(index), "--iters", str(args.iters), "--delay-ms", str(args.delay_ms)] + (["--probe"] if probe else []) out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True) text = out.stdout + out.stderr info = {"hip": next((l[7:] for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("HIPVER ")), "?"), "probe": next((json.loads(l[6:]) for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("PROBE ")), None)} res = next((json.loads(l[7:]) for l in out.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("RESULT ")), None) if res is not None: info["verdict"] = "WRONG OUTPUT" if res["mismatches"] else "ok" info["detail"] = f"output matches reference; plan B call {res['plan_b_ms']} ms" \ if not res["mismatches"] else f"{res['mismatches']}/{args.iters} iterations differ" elif "Memory access fault" in text or "illegal memory access" in text or out.returncode < 0: info["verdict"] = "GPU FAULT" fault = next((l.strip() for l in text.splitlines() if "Memory access fault" in l), "") info["detail"] = fault or "illegal memory access" else: info["verdict"] = "error" info["detail"] = (text.strip().splitlines() or [f"rc={out.returncode}"])[-1][:100] return info def main(): p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter) p.add_argument("--streams", type=int, default=1, help="create this many non-blocking streams; >1 runs the race on each") p.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=5) p.add_argument("--delay-ms", type=float, default=50.0) p.add_argument("--child", choices=["race", "synced", "fixed"], help=argparse.SUPPRESS) p.add_argument("--index", type=int, default=0, help=argparse.SUPPRESS) p.add_argument("--probe", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS) args = p.parse_args() if args.child: child(args.child, args.streams, args.index, args.iters, args.delay_ms, args.probe) return env = " ".join(f"{k}={os.environ[k]}" for k in ("GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES", "DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES", "AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY") if k in os.environ) or "runtime defaults" if args.streams == 1: rows = [(m, run_child(args, m, 1, 0, False)) for m in ("race", "synced", "fixed")] print(f"HIP {rows[0][1]['hip']}, {env}, {args.delay_ms:.0f} ms delay, {args.iters} iterations") print(f"{'mode':<7} | {'result':<12} | detail") print("-" * 72) for m, r in rows: print(f"{m:<7} | {r['verdict']:<12} | {r['detail']}") return rows = [(i, run_child(args, "race", args.streams, i, True)) for i in range(args.streams)] hip_ver = rows[0][1]["hip"] print(f"HIP {hip_ver}, {env}, race mode, {args.streams} streams, " f"{args.delay_ms:.0f} ms delay, {args.iters} iterations") print(f"{'prefill stream':>14} | {'shares null-stream queue':>24} | {'result':<12} | detail") print("-" * 96) for i, r in rows: shares = "?" if r["probe"] is None else ("yes" if i in r["probe"] else "no") print(f"{i:>14} | {shares:>24} | {r['verdict']:<12} | {r['detail']}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
### Exact error On most ranks at once, with the address in 0x6c000-0x6f000: ```text Warning: Queue error - HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: ...) on address 0x6c000. Reason: Write access to a read-only page. terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError' what(): CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered ``` The batch vLLM dumps at the fault always has the same shape: one new, unchunked ~8.1k-token prefill plus 29-30 decodes (e.g. `num_scheduled_tokens` sum 8204 = 8175 + 29 x 1). That step is larger than `max_cudagraph_capture_size`, so it runs without CUDA graphs. ## When the error disappears Each row changes one thing relative to the reproduction (same stream, seed 4, 1024 prompts): | Change | Result | | --- | --- | | none | fault at request 111 | | `--enforce-eager` | fault at request 111 (CUDA graphs not involved) | | FP8 ASM prefill disabled (`_fp8_mla_prefill_supported()` forced to `False`) | 1024/1024 | | `--no-async-scheduling` | 1024/1024 | | `torch.cuda.synchronize()` immediately before `get_ps_metadata_v1` | 1024/1024 (x2) | | real LSE buffer passed to the decode kernel (`final_lse` non-null) | fault at request 78 (decode not involved) | | instrumentation that synchronizes after every MLA call | 1024/1024 (the race is hidden) | | ROCm 7.2 image, same code | no fault observed end to end (the standalone reproduction does fault) | | `AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=1` (runtime: copies wait for already-queued work) | 1024/1024 (the same stream faulted at request 78 without it) | | `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1` (runtime: every stream shares one hardware queue) | 1024/1024 (same stream) | | proposed fix (stream-ordered metadata update, see below) | 1024/1024 on every stream above | `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING` makes no difference with an FP8 KV cache. `use_gluon_decode()` returns `False` for any quantized KV cache before the setting is read, so "asm" and "auto" run the same kernels. ## Root cause 1. One persistent set of FP8 prefill PS metadata buffers is allocated per builder ([`_init_fp8_prefill_ps_buffers`, L785-L804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L785-L804)). 2. Every batch with an unchunked prefill rewrites them via `aiter.get_ps_metadata_v1` ([`_build_fp8_prefill_ps_metadata`, L901-L918](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L901-L918), called from [`build()`, L1315-L1320](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L1315-L1320)). Each step's metadata only references the shared buffers ([L937-L941](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L937-L941)). 3. `get_ps_metadata_v1` plans on the host and copies the result into the caller's device tensors with blocking `hipMemcpy` and no stream ([aiter `v1_2_host.cuh` L395-L418](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/v0.1.22.post1/csrc/kernels/mla/metadata/v1_2_host.cuh#L395-L418)). 4. The consumers, `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` and `mla_reduce_v1`, are launched asynchronously once per layer ([L1799-L1832](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L1799-L1832)). 5. The builder's `.item()` sync on `reduce_indptr[-1]` comes after the rewrite, so it cannot prevent it ([L930-L931](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L930-L931)). Decode is not affected: its plan comes from `get_mla_metadata_v1`, a device-side kernel on the current stream ([L1221](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/29468dde8b515031dc6d4d9d06bf0a2fa0442098/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/rocm_aiter_mla.py#L1221)). ### Why ROCm 7.2 does not show it end to end ROCm 7.2 has the same race and hides it by accident: in practice, its plan copy waits behind GPU work that is already queued. **Same rules on both versions.** - vLLM runs these kernels on a non-blocking stream it creates, on both runtimes. - A stream-less `hipMemcpy` waits only for the null stream and for blocking streams, never for non-blocking ones. The code path is the same in the two HIP runtime builds shipped in these images (`ROCm/rocm-systems` `af70edc9` for 7.2 and `25e14349` for ROCm 10, per vLLM's `Dockerfile.rocm_base` / `Dockerfile.rock_base`). - In a two-stream test, `get_ps_metadata_v1` returns on both versions while a kernel on a vLLM-style stream is still running, and the new bytes are already visible. - The standalone reproduction above faults on both. **The window opens equally often.** With a non-synchronizing counter, about 7–11% of prefill plan updates start while the previous step's prefill is still queued, on both images. **The difference is how long the copy takes when it overlaps.** We timed `get_ps_metadata_v1` in the server, with no added synchronization: | When the previous prefill is still queued | ROCm 10 | ROCm 7.2 | | --- | --- | --- | | Mean plan-update time | ~0.8 ms | ~105–133 ms | | Updates that returned only after that prefill finished | almost none | about two thirds | | Mean plan-update time with no overlap | ~0.9 ms | ~14.5 ms | On ROCm 7.2 the copy usually sits behind in-flight work, including the prefill still reading the plan. On ROCm 10 it lands immediately, which is the fault. **Why a blocking copy can end up waiting for unrelated work.** - The first of AITER's five copies, `work_indptr` (1,028 bytes), is below HIP's 16 KiB blit threshold (`GPU_FORCE_BLIT_COPY_SIZE`). The runtime therefore runs it as a small copy kernel on the null stream's hardware queue. The other four copies use the SDMA engines. - Hardware queues are in order. A process with more streams than hardware queues (default 4 per GPU) shares them. - If the null stream's queue holds in-flight work, that copy waits for it. Because every `hipMemcpy` blocks, the whole plan update waits too. Forcing every stream onto one hardware queue on ROCm 10 (`GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=1`) removes the fault, and so does `AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=1`. Both are on a stream that faults at request 78 otherwise. **Changing ROCm 7.2's queue assignment makes it crash.** Unpatched ROCm 7.2, same request streams: | ROCm 7.2 | Result | | --- | --- | | defaults | 1024/1024, 2048/2048 | | `DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=1` | crash at request 117 (x3, on 2 machines, including the stock image); plan update now ~0.8 ms | | `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16` | crash at request 111 (x2, on 2 machines, stock image) | | `DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=1` + proposed fix | 1024/1024 | | `GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=16` + proposed fix | 1024/1024 | Both crashes are `hipErrorIllegalAddress` with the usual crash batch, at the same request numbers where ROCm 10 faults. A single-GPU version of the standalone reproduction runs the prefill on each of 12 non-blocking streams. On ROCm 7.2 defaults, only the streams that share the null stream's hardware queue are protected; with either setting, or on ROCm 10, every stream faults. Which stream shares that queue depends on the order in which streams first launch work, because HIP binds a stream to a hardware queue at first use. That is also why `DEBUG_HIP_DYNAMIC_QUEUES=0` does not protect ROCm 10 in vLLM: it still faults at request 117, because its static mapping puts the collision on other streams. Either way, correctness must not rely on this. The copy has no ordering guarantee on any ROCm version. When the stale indices stay in bounds, the prefill attention output would be silently wrong instead of faulting. We have not linked this to a measured accuracy drop: `niah_single_2` (4k at concurrency 4/32/64, 64k and 128k at concurrency 32) scored the same with and without the fix. ## How this was narrowed down - Reproduced deterministically (fixed stream, same fault request) and checked eager mode: still faults, so CUDA graphs are not involved. - Confirmed from the backend code that FP8 KV routes decode to the padded ASM persistent kernel `mla_a8w8_qh16_qseqlen1_gqaratio16_ps`, whatever the ASM padding setting. - Compared the ROCm 7.2 and ROCm 10 images: identical vLLM/AITER Python and identical ASM `.co` files. Kernel-argument layouts match their declared sizes. All compiled AITER modules and the HIP runtime differ. - Toggled one component at a time (table above). Only removing the FP8 prefill path, removing async scheduling, or ordering the metadata rewrite made the fault go away. - Checked AITER's host planner: it writes full output buffers with stream-less `hipMemcpy` (`work_info` alone is ~8.9 MB at `batch=256, max_qlen=16384`). - Verified that `get_ps_metadata_v1` accepts pinned host output tensors and produces byte-identical plans to device outputs (5 batch shapes, including the crash batch). This is what the fix relies on. - Checked which stream vLLM uses (non-blocking, on both images) and whether a stream-less `hipMemcpy` waits for queued kernels on it (no, on both runtimes). Then isolated the race in the standalone reproduction above, which faults on ROCm 7.2 too. ## Proposed fix vLLM-only: plan into two pinned host staging slots, copy to the device buffers with `copy_(non_blocking=True)` on the current stream, and reuse a slot only after its previous copy completes (CUDA event). `num_partial_tiles` then comes from the host plan, which removes a GPU sync per prefill step. Throughput is unchanged (e.g. 8k/1k concurrency 32: 1083.0 vs 1082.6 output tok/s). PR: #58887. An AITER-side follow-up (a stream-ordered host planner, or a device-side planner like decode) would make device outputs safe for all callers: [ROCm/aiter#5879](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/issues/5879). This report and the experiments behind it were produced with help from a Cursor agent. ## Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
