title: [Bug]: llama3_json streaming drops assistant content that starts with '{' but is not a tool call (non-streaming returns it)
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment (collect_env.py asserts on macOS, so summarised by hand)</summary>

```text
OS: macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Python 3.12.13, CPU only
vLLM: 0.30.0 (pure-Python parser code from the manylinux wheel), and main @ 3b4566c5cf014605de6aeab6eb831b4f20511c17
transformers 5.17.0, tokenizers 0.23.2, torch 2.14.0 (CPU), partial-json-parser 0.2.1.1.post7
```

Parser-only bug: no GPU, weights or server needed. Tokenizer: `unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct@99cd0d2c`.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Llama3JsonToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` decides between content and tool call from the first character only (`current_text.startswith("{")` or `<|python_tag|>`), and never falls back. So streaming and non-streaming disagree on three kinds of plain Llama 3.x output:

1. **A plain answer that starts with `{` but is not a call** (a JSON answer, `{}`, `{"a": 1} is a dict`). Non-streaming returns it as `content`. Streaming returns `content=None` and no tool calls, so the answer disappears.
2. **A call with empty arguments.** Non-streaming gives `arguments='{}'`, streaming gives `arguments=''`.
3. **Text before the call** (`Let me check. {"name": ...}`; with the default `skip_special_tokens=True` this is also what a `<|python_tag|>` call looks like after detokenization). Non-streaming returns the call and drops the text (the docstring says surrounding text is ignored). Streaming returns everything, JSON included, as `content`, with no tool call.

Case 1 is the most serious one: a client that streams loses the model's whole reply.

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer
from vllm.tool_parsers.llama_tool_parser import Llama3JsonToolParser

tok = get_tokenizer("unsloth/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct",
                    revision="99cd0d2c829e92a67c844f9144c2509632e5c87f")
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {
    "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}}},
         {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time", "parameters": {
    "type": "object", "properties": {}}}}]
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
                            tools=tools, tool_choice="auto")

def stream(text):
    """One token per delta."""
    ids = tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
    p = Llama3JsonToolParser(tok, req.tools)
    prev_text, content, calls = "", "", {}
    for i in range(len(ids)):
        cur_text = tok.decode(ids[: i + 1])
        d = p.extract_tool_calls_streaming(prev_text, cur_text, cur_text[len(prev_text):],
                                           ids[:i], ids[: i + 1], ids[i : i + 1], req)
        if d and d.content:
            content += d.content
        for tc in (d.tool_calls if d else []):
            c = calls.setdefault(tc.index, ["", ""])
            c[0] += (tc.function.name or "") if tc.function else ""
            c[1] += (tc.function.arguments or "") if tc.function else ""
        prev_text = cur_text
    return content or None, [tuple(c) for c in calls.values()]

for text in ['{"capital": "Paris", "country": "France"}',
             '{"a": 1} is a dict',
             '{}',
             '{"name": "get_time", "parameters": {}}',
             'Let me check. {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Tokyo"}}']:
    info = Llama3JsonToolParser(tok, req.tools).extract_tool_calls(text, req)
    print(repr(text))
    print("  non-streaming:", info.content, [(t.function.name, t.function.arguments) for t in info.tool_calls])
    print("  streaming    :", *stream(text))
```

Output on 0.30.0 and on main @ 3b4566c (identical; the `KeyError: 'name'` log lines are omitted):

```text
'{"capital": "Paris", "country": "France"}'
  non-streaming: {"capital": "Paris", "country": "France"} []
  streaming    : None []
'{"a": 1} is a dict'
  non-streaming: {"a": 1} is a dict []
  streaming    : None []
'{}'
  non-streaming: {} []
  streaming    : None []
'{"name": "get_time", "parameters": {}}'
  non-streaming: None [('get_time', '{}')]
  streaming    : None [('get_time', '')]
'Let me check. {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Tokyo"}}'
  non-streaming: None [('get_weather', '{"city": "Tokyo"}')]
  streaming    : Let me check. {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {"city": "Tokyo"}} []
```

Larger deltas (4 tokens, or the whole output in one delta) give the same result for cases 1 and 3.

**Expected:** streaming returns the same content and tool calls as non-streaming. For case 1, when the buffered `{...}` turns out not to be a call (no `name` key, or text after the object), it should be flushed as content. For case 3, the text before the call should be content in both modes, as SGLang's Llama 3.2 detector test expects ([`test_llama32_detector.py#L84-L88`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/94602c9c2b7cbdb8efd5c52802dac6a1c180089e/test/registered/unit/function_call/test_llama32_detector.py#L84-L88)).

**Related:** I applied the open PR #51577 (llama3_json on the ParserEngine) to main @ 3b4566c, and it fixes all five cases in both modes: content is kept in case 1, `'{}'` in case 2, and `content='Let me check.'` plus the call in case 3. So this issue may simply be tracked by that PR. #48294 (whole call in one delta) is a different bug in the same function. [sglang#35562](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35562) is the same class of bug in SGLang.

Fixtures (template-rendered or taken from the linked tests):
- [`llama/l3-json-answer-not-a-call`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/d27dceba4fdbef4981f0144eb0ae2e1766d5ffc3/fixtures/llama/l3-render.jsonl#L10)
- [`llama/l3-empty-arguments`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/d27dceba4fdbef4981f0144eb0ae2e1766d5ffc3/fixtures/llama/l3-render.jsonl#L4)
- [`llama/l3-bug-leading-json-object-in-content`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/d27dceba4fdbef4981f0144eb0ae2e1766d5ffc3/fixtures/llama/imported.jsonl#L15)
- [`llama/l3-sglang-text-before-python-tag`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/d27dceba4fdbef4981f0144eb0ae2e1766d5ffc3/fixtures/llama/imported.jsonl#L8)

I found this with an automated conformance harness. The report was drafted with AI assistance, and I verified the repro above by running it on both versions.

Found by canitoolcall (https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall), an offline conformance suite for tool-call parsers.

title: [Bug][Frontend]: Anthropic /v1/messages always hoists inline system messages because merge detection checks the CLI --chat-template (None) instead of the model's template
body:
### Your current environment

`main` @ 73a78e6f1f. `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --reasoning-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47` (no `--chat-template`), with Claude Code 2.1.281 connected via `/v1/messages`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

This is item 1 of #58647, split out as its own issue.

`AnthropicServingMessages.__init__` decides whether to hoist inline `role: "system"` messages by calling:

```python
self._merge_inline_system = self._detect_merge_inline_system(chat_template)
```

`chat_template` here is the **`--chat-template` CLI value**, which is `None` for almost every deployment, and `_detect_merge_inline_system` short-circuits:

```python
if not chat_template:
    return True
```

As a result, the probe that renders `[system, user, system, user]` never runs against the template that is actually used, which comes from the tokenizer. **Every deployment that relies on the model's own template goes down the merge path**, including models whose templates handle inline system messages correctly (GLM-5.3 is one). The "preserve in place" branch added in #46025 only runs when a user passes `--chat-template` explicitly.

The merge path (`_convert_system_message`) appends every inline system message to the leading system block. Claude Code sends a new inline system message almost every turn (`<total_tokens>N tokens left</total_tokens>`). So the leading block changes on each request, and everything after it, i.e. the whole conversation, misses the prefix cache. It also changes semantics: a mid-conversation instruction becomes part of the global system prompt.

#### Reproducer (offline, tokenizer only)

The script builds Claude Code-shaped consecutive turns, runs each one through `to_chat_completion_request`, renders it with GLM-5.3-Flash's template, and counts how many prompt tokens turn N+1 shares with turn N. That count is the best possible prefix-cache hit.

<details><summary>repro_inline_system.py</summary>

```python
import json
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.anthropic.protocol import AnthropicMessagesRequest
from vllm.entrypoints.anthropic.serving import AnthropicServingMessages

MODEL = "zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash"
SYSTEM = [
    {"type": "text", "text": "x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=2.1.281; cch=abc"},
    {"type": "text", "text": "You are Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI." * 50},
]
TOOLS = [{"name": "Bash", "description": "Run a shell command.",
          "input_schema": {"type": "object",
                           "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}},
                           "required": ["command"]}}]


def claude_code_turn(n):
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "List the files in the repo and count them."},
            {"role": "system", "content": "# Environment\n - Platform: linux"}]
    left = 15_000_000
    for i in range(n):
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "thinking", "thinking": f"I should run step {i}.", "signature": ""},
            {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{i}", "name": "Bash",
             "input": {"command": f"ls | head -{i + 1}"}}]})
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": [
            {"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": f"toolu_{i}",
             "content": "\n".join(f"file_{j}.py" for j in range(i + 1))}]})
        left -= 173 * (i + 1)
        msgs.append({"role": "system",
                     "content": f"<total_tokens>{left} tokens left</total_tokens>"})
    return {"model": MODEL, "max_tokens": 32000, "system": SYSTEM,
            "tools": TOOLS, "messages": msgs}


def render(tok, body, merge):
    req = AnthropicServingMessages.to_chat_completion_request(
        AnthropicMessagesRequest.model_validate(body), merge_inline_system=merge)
    messages = [m if isinstance(m, dict) else m.model_dump() for m in req.messages]
    for m in messages:  # chat_utils parses tool-call arguments before rendering
        for tc in m.get("tool_calls") or []:
            tc["function"]["arguments"] = json.loads(tc["function"]["arguments"])
    tools = [t.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for t in req.tools or []]
    text = tok.apply_chat_template(messages, tools=tools, tokenize=False,
                                   add_generation_prompt=True)
    return tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)


def shared(a, b):
    n = 0
    while n < min(len(a), len(b)) and a[n] == b[n]:
        n += 1
    return n


tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
for label, merge in {
    "today: detect(None)": AnthropicServingMessages._detect_merge_inline_system(None),
    "detect(tokenizer template)":
        AnthropicServingMessages._detect_merge_inline_system(tok.chat_template),
}.items():
    print(f"=== {label} -> merge_inline_system={merge}")
    prompts = [render(tok, claude_code_turn(n), merge) for n in range(1, 5)]
    for i in range(1, len(prompts)):
        k = shared(prompts[i - 1], prompts[i])
        print(f"turn {i}->{i + 1}: shared {k}/{len(prompts[i - 1])} "
              f"({k / len(prompts[i - 1]):.1%})")
```
</details>

Output:

```
=== today: detect(None) -> merge_inline_system=True
turn 1->2: shared 671/709 (94.6%)
turn 2->3: shared 684/751 (91.1%)
turn 3->4: shared 697/798 (87.3%)
=== detect(tokenizer template) -> merge_inline_system=False
turn 1->2: shared 712/712 (100.0%)
turn 2->3: shared 756/756 (100.0%)
turn 3->4: shared 805/805 (100.0%)
```

In the merged case, the rendered prompt splits right where the `<total_tokens>` messages pile up in the leading system block, before the first `<|user|>`:

```
...<total_tokens>14999481 tokens left</total_tokens><total_tokens>14998962 tokens left</total_tokens ^ ><total_tokens>14998270 tokens left</total_tokens><|user|>List the files...
```

The shared prefix never grows past the tools block plus the base system prompt. Every token after that is recomputed on each turn, so the cost grows with the length of the session.

I ran the same measurement on captured Claude Code 2.1.281 traffic against GLM-5.3-Flash (4 consecutive main-loop requests, about 20k-token prompts). The results match: today the shared prefix stays at about 17.7k tokens (tools + system prompt, 89–90%) on every turn that adds an inline system message. With detection against the tokenizer template it is 100% on every turn.

#### Expected

`_detect_merge_inline_system` should run against the **resolved** chat template (the tokenizer's `chat_template`, or the renderer's resolved template), not the CLI override. Models whose templates accept non-leading system messages should then keep them in place.

#### Notes / related

- The same pattern is used in `vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/render/serving.py:60`.
- `test_anthropic_messages_conversion.py` asserts `_detect_merge_inline_system(None) is True`, which encodes the current behavior.
- Fixing detection alone does not help templates that really do require system-first (e.g. Qwen's `loop.first` guard): they will still merge and still miss the cache. Those need the fold-into-adjacent-turn approach discussed in #53393. Some templates (MiniMax-M3, the DeepSeek-V3.2 encoder, see #46710 / #53737) also mishandle in-place system messages, so they may need their own fallback.
- Related: #53393, #46710, #48874, #41114. Competing PRs listed in #58647: #53501, #56520, #52978, #47681.

*This issue was drafted with AI assistance (Claude Code); I ran the reproducer and checked the output above.*

title: [Tracking] Gemma4 AITER QK-norm+RoPE+KVCache fusion + RoPE IR-op migration (ROCm)
body:
Umbrella tracker: Gemma4 QK-norm + RoPE (head_dim 512) fusion on ROCm/AITER and CUDA, plus the RoPE → vLLM IR-op migration that drops the `+rotary_embedding` requirement (#28042).

**Owner:** @mpashkovskii

### Tracked PRs

- [ ] #53918 — AITER `fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache` for Gemma4 (head_dim 512 + V-norm); depends on #58838
- [ ] #53115 — head_dim 512 for the non-AITER `fused_qk_norm_rope` path (CUDA / `TRITON_ATTN`)
- [ ] #58838 — port base RoPE to a vLLM IR op so the fusion matches without `+rotary_embedding` (draft)
- [x] ROCm/aiter#5027 — AITER kernel: head_dim 512 + weightless V-norm (merged, cross-repo)

### Related work

RoPE-to-IR has been attempted before: **#38756** ("Port RoPE ops to IR") tracked it, with **#43199** (@wxsIcey) and its predecessors **#39488 / #41773 / #42264** carrying the implementation. That series is **closed and unmerged** (last state: merge conflicts, `mergeable_state: dirty`), and RoPE is still **not** an IR op on current `main`.

#58838 revives that direction but differs materially:

- rebased on current `main`, conflict-free;
- **keeps `MatcherRotaryEmbedding`** instead of deleting it — current `main` gained the AITER `QkNormRopeKvCacheFusionPass` (#53918) *after* #43199 was written, and that pass depends on the matcher;
- **completes the ROCm/AITER path** (adds an `aiter` IR provider, decouples the AITER dispatch from `RotaryEmbedding.enabled()`);
- scope limited to the base `RotaryEmbedding` (Neox / GPT-J); `DeepseekScalingRotaryEmbedding`, mRoPE, flashinfer, and the `key=None` cross-layer-KV-sharing path are left for follow-ups.

Motivating bug: **#28042** — RoPE only matched the QK-norm+RoPE fusion when registered as a custom op.

title: [Bug] Hybrid mamba prefix-cache hit reads out of bounds: add_request seeds the state index with cache_config.block_size after it was lowered below mamba_block_size (Xid 31 / illegal memory access)
body:
**Summary.** `MambaHybridModelState.add_request` seeds the running mamba state slot as
`(num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size`, but by the time it runs, `EngineCore._initialize_kv_caches` has already reassigned `cache_config.block_size` to `min(block_size of prefix-cacheable groups)`. For hybrid models that carry an extra attention group with a small block size (here: a DFlash2/EAGLE-style drafter group with sliding-window spec, block 64 or 1024), that minimum is far below `cache_config.mamba_block_size` (7168 here). The seed therefore indexes the mamba block table in the wrong units, and `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel` → `_copy_mamba_state_block` reads `block_table[src_col]` past the row width without a bounds check. Above the row width this is an illegal memory access (Xid 31, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`); below it, the request silently restores the KDA/mamba state from an unrelated block.

**Where.**
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`, `add_request`: `(new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size` (main, ~L70-77).
- `vllm/v1/engine/core.py`, `_initialize_kv_caches`: `vllm_config.cache_config.block_size = min(participating ...)` (main, ~L298-305). The comment there already notes that a small-block group "would otherwise drag the global block_size below the real allocator block size and desync it from mamba"; the min still includes any prefix-cacheable attention group with a smaller block.
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: `preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel` uses the seed as `src_col`; `_copy_mamba_state_block` loads `block_table_base + src_col` with no check against the row width. Mamba state blocks and the block-table row width (`cdiv(max_model_len, mamba_block_size) + num_speculative_blocks`) are in units of `mamba_block_size`.

**Environment.** vLLM `v0.1.dev20051+g487ecf187` (container image from github.com/gitcommit90/glm-5.3-one-spark), GLM-5.3-Flash (hybrid: MLA sparse attention + KDA linear attention), DFlash2 speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens=5`), `--enable-prefix-caching` (so `mamba_cache_mode=align`), `max_num_seqs=1`, `max_num_batched_tokens=7168`, `mamba_block_size=7168`, V2 model runner, TP=1 (UniProcExecutor, so the worker sees the reassigned config), DGX Spark GB10.

**Reproduction (deterministic).** Threshold model `crash ⇔ (hit_tokens - 1) // small_block >= row_width` matched 8/8 observations:

| max_model_len | drafter block | row width | cached prefix (tokens) | seed | result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 262144 | 64 | 42 | 7168 | 111 | crash |
| 262144 | 1024 | 42 | 7168 / 28672 / 43008 | 6 / 27 / 41 | no crash, wrong state restored |
| 262144 | 1024 | 42 | 57344 | 55 | crash |
| 524288 | 1024 | 79 | 93184 | 90 | crash |

Steps: send prompt A (>= 8 full mamba blocks, e.g. 57k tokens), then A + a different question. The second request fails within <1 s with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` (reported at the first sync point, e.g. `flash_linear_attention/ops/index.py prepare_chunk_indices .tolist()` or `np_to_pinned_tensor`), and `dmesg` shows `NVRM: Xid 31 ... MMU Fault ... FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`.

**Fix (verified).** Divide by the mamba block size:

```diff
-                (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.block_size
+                (new_req_data.num_computed_tokens - 1) // self.cache_config.mamba_block_size
```

`mamba_attn.py` already computes the same quantity from `kv_cache_spec.block_size`. With the one-line change: 8-, 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete, needle-in-a-haystack answers on warm (cached) requests are identical to cold ones at 100k and 250k tokens (5/5 needles each), and warm TTFT drops from 139 s to 8.7 s at 100k. A needle placed inside the last partial scheduler chunk before the block boundary is also retrieved on warm requests.

Alternatively/additionally, `core.py` could exclude sliding-window drafter groups from the `min(...)` (as it already excludes opt-out groups), which would also stop `_mamba_block_aligned_split` from chunking prefill at multiples of the drafter block (6144 instead of 7168 here).

**Why this is easy to miss.** With `max_num_seqs >= 2` the out-of-range read often lands in another request's row (a valid block id), so there is no fault, only a silently wrong recurrent state; with TP >= 2 the workers keep a config copy from before the reassignment. Symptoms then look like "model loops / degrades after a while under load" rather than a crash.

**Before/after on the same input.** Prompt A of 57 344 tokens (8 full mamba blocks), then A + a different question:
- without the fix: HTTP 500 after 0.2 s, `Xid 31` in dmesg (02:43, `crash-BLOCKS8-*.log`);
- with the fix: warm request completes in 11.7 s, 50 176 tokens served from cache.

**Validation with the fix (same container build, `max_model_len` 262144 and 524288):** 13-, 34- and 63-block prefix hits complete; multi-needle recall on warm (cached) requests equals cold at 100k, 250k and 450k tokens (5/5 each; warm TTFT 8.7 s vs 139 s cold at 100k); a needle placed inside the last partial scheduler chunk before the block boundary is also retrieved on the warm request; a 3-hour soak with 57 multi-turn conversation turns (every turn a prefix hit, contexts up to 184k tokens) plus fresh 41k–354k-token prompts: 133/133 requests OK, zero Xid, no memory drift.

Happy to open a PR if you'd like the fix in that form.

title: [RFC]: Native span pooling for contextual chunk embeddings
body:
## Motivation

Retrieval applications often index paragraphs separately. Encoding each paragraph in isolation loses cross-paragraph context: “its maintenance team” may refer to a company named in an earlier paragraph. [Late chunking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.04701) encodes the document first, then pools token representations within each chunk.

vLLM already returns token embeddings. For suitable models, an application can disable token normalization with `use_activation=False`, export the representations and pool them correctly outside the worker. This proposal adds a native way to return only the requested chunk vectors, with a shared request contract and worker-side aggregation.

The existing [long-text embedding feature](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/22280) splits an oversized input into independent forwards and combines their outputs into one document vector. Here, multiple chunk vectors come from one shared document encoding, within the model's context limit. The algorithm is established; the proposed contribution is its integration into vLLM's pooling path.

## Proposed change

Add an opt-in span-pooling task, tentatively named `span_embed`, through `LLM.encode` and the existing `/pooling` endpoint. The default embedding APIs keep their current behavior.

### Request semantics

For the first release, use the existing token-ID input path. Each request contains one complete, unpadded token sequence and one or more ordered, non-overlapping ranges. This makes the worker's input unambiguous and avoids introducing a second server-side tokenization path.

Illustrative request; the task and `token_spans` field are proposed:

```json
{
  "model": "span-enabled-encoder",
  "task": "span_embed",
  "input": [101, 2023, 2003, 1037, 7953, 1012, 102],
  "add_special_tokens": false,
  "token_spans": [[0, 4], [4, 7]]
}
```

Token IDs are illustrative; callers must use the served model's tokenizer and pinned revision.

- Ranges are zero-based and half-open: `[start, end)`. They refer to the exact submitted token sequence. Reject empty, reversed, overlapping or out-of-bounds ranges, and enforce a server-side span-count limit.
- All input tokens provide context. Only tokens within each range participate in its mean. Special tokens and instructions are included if their positions are selected; the engine never silently includes or excludes them.
- Require `add_special_tokens=false` and reject request/config options that would truncate, pad, rewrite or split this input. Ordinary internal batch padding is not part of the sequence or its ranges. Oversized inputs fail validation.
- Return one `[K, D]` matrix in the existing pooling response, where row `i` corresponds to input span `i`. Count input tokens once per document. Concurrent requests remain independently batched by the engine.

Ship a text-to-token example with the first release so users can start from text and paragraph boundaries. It uses the same pinned tokenizer as the deployment, tokenizes the complete model input once, and sends those exact IDs with the resolved ranges. It rejects boundaries inside a token. The late-chunking reference example follows the paper's convention of including prefix tokens in the first chunk and suffix tokens in the last. A content-only example must be identified as a different convention. A text/character-span server API can follow once this operation is established.

### Shared implementation, explicit model support

Implement the reduction once in the common pooler layer:

```text
full-document model forward
  -> span means, accumulated in FP32
  -> validated model-specific embedding head
  -> K output vectors, copied from the worker
```

The head includes the supported projection, dtype conversion and normalization in the model's verified order. We must not move nonlinear transformations across the mean or assume that exported token embeddings always equal raw hidden states.

Start with an explicitly enabled bidirectional MEAN-pooling model. `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1`, at the revision pinned by existing vLLM tests, is the initial integration candidate; its HF compatibility constraint remains in place. MiniLM provides inexpensive reference coverage. Additional models reuse the reducer but require validation of their head and input conventions. Unsupported models fail before scheduling. LAST/CLS models are not automatically enabled.

The integration covers:

1. Pooling request/offline input validation and typed `token_spans` in `PoolingParams`.
2. Task registration, parameter defaults, model capability reporting and `DispatchPooler` selection. A compatible head must explicitly support the new task; existing heads must not advertise support globally.
3. Request metadata transport and batch slicing, preserving the association between each request's ranges and hidden states through reordering and task grouping.
4. Reduction before worker output copying, using the existing variable-row pooling output. Extend existing pooling tests and examples.

This uses the current scheduler and model forward path. Initial encoder targets keep their existing restrictions on prefix caching and chunked prefill. Documents must fit a full supported context. Automatic segmentation, cross-window context, decoder models and multimodal inputs are outside the first release.

### Alternatives and related work

A correct token-export/client-pooling path is the first baseline. An IO processor can also aggregate outputs before the HTTP response, although token-level worker output has already been produced. A custom model pooler combined with a plugin can perform aggregation inside the worker too.

The argument for native support is a reusable contract and validated model integration, rather than requiring separate model wrappers. Plugins are a legitimate alternative: [#37344](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37344#issuecomment-4080081406) recommended them for custom span-shaped outputs. I would like feedback on whether this use case warrants a native task.

This differs from existing multi-head embedding output and late-interaction scoring. It also differs from [#56916](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56916), which concerns capturing hidden states during response generation. External demand exists, for example [TEI #434](https://github.com/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference/issues/434); vLLM users' models and workloads would help establish the priority here.

### Validation and delivery

A local CPU probe combined a real MiniLM encoder with vLLM's pooler/head components on four documents and eleven spans. The component results matched direct reference calculations. This is feasibility evidence, not an end-to-end implementation or a performance result.

Implementation acceptance should cover:

- Numerical agreement with a fixed-revision HF reference using identical token IDs, ranges and head semantics, including special-token selection.
- Online/offline agreement, mixed-length and mixed-task batching, invalid inputs, context limits and unchanged existing embedding results.
- Comparison with correctly configured token export plus client pooling: worker-output bytes, host memory and end-to-end latency at matched workloads. A worker-side plugin can establish whether native integration adds any overhead, rather than assuming it must be faster.
- A representative retrieval comparison with independent-chunk encoding, reporting gains and regressions. [Subsequent evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16974) finds task-dependent effects; this is an optional capability, not a universal retrieval upgrade.

Reducing output from `N × D` to `K × D` values does not reduce the full-document attention cost or establish an end-to-end speedup.

I propose three implementation steps: the shared reducer and offline reference tests; online request integration plus the text-to-token example; then end-to-end validation and documentation for the first supported model. I would like to drive the implementation and maintain this path.

## Feedback period

Initial feedback through October 2, 2026; discussion can continue afterward. The main questions are whether native support is preferable to a plugin, whether the token-range contract is suitable, and which initial model/workload users would actually deploy. Task naming and exact field placement can be settled in review.

## CC list

cc @noooop @DarkLight1337. I would appreciate your thoughts on the pooling API and whether this belongs in core or a plugin.

```
  TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
  TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

  The V1 engine core silently deadlocks under concurrent load using default configuration. The API server remains healthy (/health returns 200, /metrics responds), but zero tokens are generated. Requests stay in "running" state indefinitely and
   the engine never recovers without a pod restart.

  vLLM serve command:
```
  vllm serve "$MODEL_DIR" \
      --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
      --dtype bfloat16 \
      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
      --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
      --max-model-len 16384 \
      --max-num-seqs 128 \
      --quantization fp8 \
      --trust-remote-code \
      --enable-prefix-caching \
      --async-scheduling \
      --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
```

  How to reproduce:

  1. Deploy vLLM with the configuration above
  2. Send concurrent requests (8-64 concurrency) — works fine initially
  3. Under sustained load or after a brief spike, the engine freezes
  4. No specific error triggers it — no OOM, no CUDA error, no validation error

  Engine log sequence showing the deadlock:
```
  13:57:45  Avg prompt throughput: 2598.6 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 1684.2 tokens/s, Running: 2 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 0.3%, Prefix cache hit rate: 96.9%
  13:57:55  Avg prompt throughput: 83.6 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 1.8 tokens/s, Running: 11 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 1.3%, Prefix cache hit rate: 96.9%
  13:58:05  Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 11 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 1.3%, Prefix cache hit rate: 96.9%
```
  After 13:58:05, throughput stays at 0.0 permanently. Running count stays at 11. KV cache stays at 1.3%. The engine never recovers.

### Key observations:

  - Not resource exhaustion: Only 11/128 request slots used, 1.3% KV cache
  - API server alive: /health returns 200, /metrics responds
  - Engine core frozen: Zero tokens generated, forward pass never executes
  - Affects arbitrary request counts: Seen with 11, 124, and other counts
  - Does not self-recover: Requires pod restart
  - --request-timeout does not help: Engine core is frozen, can't enforce timeouts

  Investigation — deadlock tied to CUDA graph code paths:

  Systematic testing to isolate the trigger:
```
  ┌──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              Config              │               Result               │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Default V1 + async-scheduling    │ DEADLOCK                           │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Default V1 + no async-scheduling │ DEADLOCK                           │
  ├──────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Default V1 + --enforce-eager     │ Didn't run enough but ~8x slower (not viable) │
  └──────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘
```

  Incident 1 (nightly build): During a production spike, autoscaler scaled from 6→20→6 replicas. Two surviving replicas entered deadlock with 123-124 running requests each, stayed frozen 4+ hours until manual restart.

  Incident 2 (v0.17.1 stable): Same deadlock reproduced within minutes of a load test. Single replica, low concurrency (8→16 ramp). Froze at 11 running requests. No autoscaling involved.

  Current workaround: --enforce-eager prevents the deadlock but with ~8x throughput regression, making it unviable for production. Restarting affected replicas is the only practical mitigation.

  - I have asked the chatbot living at docs.vllm.ai

title: [Bug]: Multimodal models fail to load on ROCm/RDNA4 (gfx1201) — `CUDA error: invalid argument` in `vit_torch_sdpa_wrapper` encoder attention
body:
---

## Summary

On vLLM 0.25.1 / ROCm 7.15, loading a multimodal model on AMD Radeon AI PRO
R9700 (RDNA4, gfx1201) fails during model initialization inside the vision
encoder attention path. Every worker rank fails identically. Text-only models on
the same build, same hardware, same launch path load and serve fine.

## Environment

- vLLM: `0.25.1+rocm715` (built from tag `v0.25.1`, commit `752a3a5044`)
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+rocm7.15.0a20260721`
- ROCm: 7.15 (TheRock nightly, `rocm-sdk` wheels, `gfx1201` device package)
- Triton: `3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.15.0a20260721`
- GPU: 6x AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201 / RDNA4), 32 GB each
- OS: Fedora 43 container, host Fedora 43
- Model: `cyankiwi/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit`
  (resolves to `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`)
- Launch: `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline-parallel-size 3
  --distributed-executor-backend ray`

## Traceback

```
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 136, in forward
File "vllm/model_executor/custom_op.py", line 151, in forward_hip
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mm_encoder_attention.py", line 731, in forward_cuda
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mm_encoder_attention.py", line 523, in _forward_sdpa
    output = vit_torch_sdpa_wrapper(
File "vllm/v1/attention/ops/vit_attn_wrappers.py", line 272, in vit_torch_sdpa_wrapper
File "torch/_ops.py", line 1269, in __call__
File "vllm/v1/attention/ops/vit_attn_wrappers.py", line 242, in torch_sdpa_wrapper
    context_layer = torch.cat(outputs, dim=1)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: invalid argument
```

Note the path: `custom_op.forward_hip` → `mm_encoder_attention.forward_cuda` →
`_forward_sdpa` → `vit_torch_sdpa_wrapper`. The HIP dispatch lands in the
`forward_cuda` implementation of encoder attention.

## What rules out the obvious alternatives

- **Not distributed / not PP-related — verified single-node.** Reproduced with
  `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend mp`, on one node,
  with no Ray and no pipeline parallelism at all: both `Worker_TP0` and
  `Worker_TP1` fail with the identical traceback. It also fails on all six ranks
  of the TP=2/PP=3 Ray configuration (`Worker_PP0_TP0` … `Worker_PP2_TP1`),
  local and remote alike.
- **Not the hardware or the build.** The same image on the same 6 GPUs loads and
  serves `Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-AWQ` (text-only, `Qwen2ForCausalLM`) with
  the identical launch command, completes startup, and answers requests. The
  only difference is the presence of a vision tower.
- **Not a device-visibility issue.** `invalid argument` here, not `invalid
  device ordinal`; the error is raised by a kernel launch inside the ViT
  attention op, after device init has succeeded on every rank.

## Reproduction

1. ROCm 7.15 + vLLM 0.25.1 on gfx1201.
2. Single node, no Ray, no PP — this is enough to reproduce:
   ```
   vllm serve cyankiwi/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit \
     --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
     --distributed-executor-backend mp \
     --gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-model-len 8192 --trust-remote-code
   ```
3. Fails during model load in the vision-encoder attention path, after the
   safetensors shards finish loading. Engine core initialization fails.

Swap to any text-only model on the same build to confirm the rest of the stack
is healthy.

## Expected

Either the ViT SDPA path works on gfx1201, or vLLM falls back to a supported
attention backend for the vision encoder on RDNA4 instead of failing to load.

## Additional context

Found while retesting
[#49826](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49826) (cross-node PP on
this hardware, which 0.25.1 fixes). This is a separate, unrelated blocker that
prevented testing that issue with a multimodal model. Happy to gather
`AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` output or test a proposed backend fallback.

title: [Bug] Deepseek-V4-Pro corruption: H100 multi-rank startup can select a FlashInfer block-FP8 path with a cold JIT cache race
body:
## Environment

- vLLM: `v0.25.1` (`752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34`)
- Container: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1`
- FlashInfer: `flashinfer-python==0.6.13`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.13`
- GPU: NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3, driver 580.105.08
- CUDA: 13.0 (`torch==2.11.0+cu130`)
- Model: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4`
- Serving topology: flat TP16 on two eight-GPU nodes
- FlashInfer issue: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4062

## Summary

vLLM 0.25.1 selects `FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel` before its pure DeepGEMM
candidate for a compatible dense block-FP8 linear. At runtime, the hybrid sends `M < 32` to
FlashInfer's `fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90`.

DeepSeek-V4-Pro's mandatory mixed warmup reaches that branch at `M=16` on every TP rank. Eight
workers on each node then cold-build the same embedded TensorRT-LLM DeepGEMM kernel against one
shared cache. FlashInfer 0.6.13 has no inter-process cache-key build lock and can fail in its CUDA
driver-library load sequence. In the captured failing launch, startup terminated with eight
copies of:

```text
CUDA error: invalid argument
```

The server starts, captures CUDA graphs, and serves coherent output when the existing vLLM
candidate gate is disabled:

```bash
export VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0
```

A direct eight-H100 operator A/B established that this is a cold-cache race, not an unsupported
`M=16` shape: the exact operator passes on all eight GPUs with per-worker JIT caches. A separate
cold stock/default-selector full-server launch also succeeded and served coherent output, which
confirms that failure is timing-dependent rather than inevitable. The final source-level patch
passed both a genuinely rebuilt-wrapper shared-cache test and a complete two-node/16-H100 TP16
server with the FlashInfer selector enabled.

## End-to-end reproduction

Start one process launcher on each eight-GPU node, with `NODE_RANK=0` on the API node,
`NODE_RANK=1` on the second node, and `HEAD_NODE` set to the API node's routable hostname. Leave
`VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER` at its default value of `1`:

```bash
ENDPOINT=--headless
if [ "$NODE_RANK" -eq 0 ]; then
  ENDPOINT="--api-server-count 1 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000"
fi

vllm serve /model \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$HEAD_NODE" --master-port 29500 \
  --max-model-len 2200 \
  --max-num-seqs 256 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 256 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  $ENDPOINT
```

The selected backends and captured failure were:

```text
Selected FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel for Fp8LinearMethod
Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend
Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
CUDA error: invalid argument
```

A separate localization launch used `--enforce-eager` and failed before CUDA graph capture, so the
error is not a graph replay failure. Operator-boundary synchronization places it in the dense
replicated `fused_wqa_wkv` projection before routed-expert MoE in that forward pass. The
reproduction command above does not require eager mode.

Repeat with:

```bash
export VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0
```

The same image, checkpoint, and launch select `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel`, retain the Marlin
NVFP4 MoE backend, complete mixed warmup and normal CUDA graph capture, and start the API. An
additional check completed eight simultaneous requests with exactly 1,024 input and 1,024 output
tokens each: 8/8 responses, zero errors, followed by a clean CUDA/illegal-memory-access scan.

## Direct operator evidence

The model projection has these exact arguments:

```text
activation:   [16, 7168], torch.bfloat16
weight:       [2048, 7168], torch.float8_e4m3fn
weight scale: [16, 56], torch.float32, stride=(56, 1), contiguous
blocks:       128x128
```

With a new shared `TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR`, eight concurrent workers reproduced `CUDA error: invalid
argument`. With the cache path made unique per local rank, every worker passed:

```text
PASS cosine=0.99966240 relative_l1=0.02618705
EXIT=0
```

The complete reproducer, lower-level source analysis, cache-hardening results, and patched
full-server validation are in the linked FlashInfer issue.

## Why vLLM reaches the race

`FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel` is an eligible CUDA block-FP8 candidate and its
`apply_block_scaled_mm` invokes `dynamic_flashinfer_deepgemm_blockscale_gemm`. That operation uses
`torch.cond` to dispatch:

```text
M < 32  -> flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90
M >= 32 -> vLLM DeepGEMM
```

This is why the mandatory `M=16` warmup is sufficient to trigger the problem before the API is
ready. The FlashInfer operator internally JIT-compiles a shape-specific SM90 cubin. All local TP
workers inherit the same default TensorRT-LLM cache root and reach the cold cache together.

The direct A/B also rules out a suspected scale handoff bug. On H100, vLLM's DeepGEMM
post-processing leaves this checkpoint's 128x128 FP32 scale tensor contiguous at `[16, 56]` with
stride `(56, 1)`. Both BF16-weight and FP8-weight forms pass when the JIT build is not raced.

## Expected behavior

A stock, supported multi-GPU vLLM configuration should not fail mandatory startup because all
local ranks cold-compile the same selected backend kernel.

## Actual behavior

The candidate passes vLLM's support checks, but FlashInfer 0.6.13 can fail during its first
multi-process JIT build. In the captured failing launch, the engine exited before serving any
request. Another stock cold launch passed, as expected for a timing-dependent race.

## Suggested resolution

The primary fix belongs in FlashInfer's embedded TensorRT-LLM compiler: serialize each cache-key
build, recheck after acquiring the lock, reject failed or empty NVCC output, require a regular
nonempty cached cubin, and propagate publication failures. The lower-level patch has completed its
exact eight-H100 rebuilt-wrapper before/after and three two-node cache-hardening tests. It also
passed a complete two-node/16-H100 TP16 server: every rank selected the FlashInfer candidate,
mixed warmup and CUDA graph capture completed, and both functional requests returned HTTP 200 with
coherent answers.

For vLLM, please consider gating this candidate for the affected FlashInfer release in
multi-worker serving, or changing its default to the pure DeepGEMM candidate until a fixed
FlashInfer version is packaged. Once the lower-level fix is available, the small-`M` optimization
can be enabled again without forcing users to know about the cache race.

## Workaround and tradeoff

```bash
export VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0
```

This removes only the hybrid FlashInfer block-FP8 candidate. It does not cap request concurrency,
dequantize the checkpoint, change KV-cache precision, or alter the separate NVFP4/Marlin MoE
operators. The tradeoff is that small-`M` dense block-FP8 operations use pure DeepGEMM instead of
FlashInfer's swap-AB path, so some decode shapes may lose an optimization.

## FlashInfer tracking

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4062

title: [Bug]: CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device when running Kimi-K3 on Ampere (A100) with vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3
body:
### Your current environment

- **GPU**: 8× NVIDIA A100 80GB (Ampere, SM 8.0) per node, 3 nodes total
- **Docker image**: `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3`
- **vLLM version** (from logs): `v0.1.dev19262+gb6bbf29dd.d20260727` (Kimi-K3 specialized build)
- **CUDA**: 13.2
- **Model**: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` 
- **OS**: Ubuntu (host)


### 🐛 Describe the bug

When launching `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (or a local copy of the weights) with the official `vllm/vllm-openai:kimi-k3` image on **NVIDIA A100 (Ampere, SM80)**, the engine fails during the memory profiling / dummy run stage with:
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
The failure occurs inside the MoE router (`gate_linear.py`) while executing `output.to(self.out_dtype)`.

This strongly suggests that some Kimi-K3 specialized CUDA kernels (especially the fused MoE router / gate linear path) in the `kimi-k3` Docker image were **not compiled for compute capability 8.0**.

title: [CI Failure]: PyTorch Fullgraph test_custom_compile_config fails with cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated
body:
### Name of failing test

`compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py::test_custom_compile_config[compilation_config8-meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-model_kwargs8]`

### Basic information

- [x] Flaky test
- [ ] Can reproduce locally
- [ ] Caused by external libraries (e.g. bug in `transformers`)

### 🧪 Describe the failing test

Job `PyTorch Fullgraph` fails during CUDA graph capture at engine startup:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 71, in ...
  cuda_graph_memory_bytes = self.model_runner.capture_model()
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", ...
  self.cudagraph_manager.capture(
File "vllm/compilation/cuda_graph.py", line 313, in __call__
  with torch.cuda.graph(
File "torch/cuda/graphs.py", line 169, in capture_end
  super().capture_end()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture
Search for `cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated' ...
```

which surfaces as:

```
FAILED compile/fullgraph/test_full_graph.py::test_custom_compile_config[compilation_config8-meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-model_kwargs8]
  - RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

`cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated` means an earlier CUDA error invalidated the capture, so the reported line is where it surfaces rather than the root cause.

Seen on https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82685, on a PR touching only `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py`.

Two existing issues mention the same CUDA error but on different paths, so this looked distinct: #40742 (Inductor autotuning calling `torch.cuda.synchronize()` at startup) and #48749 (MTP speculative decoding, `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported`). Happy to have this closed as a duplicate if it is the same underlying cause.

### 📝 History of failing test

Noticed on build 82685. Not bisected.

### CC List.

_No response_

def stop_vllm(signum, frame):
    global process
    print("\n--- 正在停止 vLLM 服务... ---")
    if process:
        process.terminate()
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=10)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            process.kill()
    sys.exit(0)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop_vllm)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop_vllm)
    start_vllm()
    while True:
        time.sleep(5)
        if process.poll() is not None:
            print("!!! vLLM 进程已退出，尝试重启...")
            start_vllm()

title: [Bug]: gpt-oss (HarmonyParser): a stray 'commentary to=assistant' header is returned as a tool call named 'assistant<|channel|>analysis'
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment (collect_env.py asserts on macOS, so summarised by hand)</summary>

```text
OS: macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Python 3.12.13, CPU only
vLLM: 0.30.0 (pure-Python parser code from the manylinux wheel), and main @ 3b4566c5cf014605de6aeab6eb831b4f20511c17
openai-harmony 0.0.8, transformers 5.17.0, torch 2.14.0 (CPU)
```

Parser-only bug: no GPU, weights or server needed. Tokenizer: `openai/gpt-oss-20b@6cee5e81`.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

gpt-oss-20b sometimes opens a turn with a stray `<|channel|>commentary to=assistant` header before its analysis channel. llama.cpp added a rule for it (ggml-org/llama.cpp#21286: "not defined in the Harmony docs, but appears to be a common generation from the 20b variant"). vLLM's Chat Completions `HarmonyParser` turns that header into a **tool call named `assistant<|channel|>analysis`**. The call's arguments are the model's reasoning, and the name is not one of the request's tools.

```python
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.parser_manager import ParserManager
from vllm.tokenizers import get_tokenizer

tok = get_tokenizer("openai/gpt-oss-20b", revision="6cee5e81ee83917806bbde320786a8fb61efebee")
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_weather", "parameters": {
    "type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}}}]
req = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}],
                            tools=tools, tool_choice="auto")
cls = ParserManager.get_parser("openai", "openai_gptoss", enable_auto_tools=True, is_harmony=True)

out = ("<|channel|>commentary to=assistant<|channel|>analysis<|message|>I'm\nthinking<|end|>"
       "<|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>Hello, world!\nWhat's up?")
ids = tok.encode(out, add_special_tokens=False)
reasoning, content, calls = cls(tok, req.tools, model_config=None).parse(
    tok.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False), req, enable_auto_tools=True, model_output_token_ids=ids)
print("reasoning :", repr(reasoning))
print("content   :", repr(content))
print("tool_calls:", [(c.name, c.arguments) for c in (calls or [])])
```

Output on 0.30.0 and on main @ 3b4566c (identical):

```text
reasoning : None
content   : "Hello, world!\nWhat's up?"
tool_calls: [('assistant<|channel|>analysis', "I'm\nthinking")]
```

Streaming (`parse_delta`, with one token per delta, the whole output in one delta, or random groups) gives the same tool call.

**Expected:** no tool call. llama.cpp's test for this string ([`test-chat.cpp` L6540-L6546](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/7fe450e19305b828c199d602c23a8337aaa1f03b/tests/test-chat.cpp#L6540-L6546)) recovers `reasoning="I'm\nthinking"` and `content="Hello, world!\nWhat's up?"`. Keeping the content and dropping the reasoning would also be reasonable. A tool call is not.

**Where:** `vllm/parser/harmony.py`, `_SegmentType.from_channel_and_recipient`. It treats any recipient accepted by `is_function_recipient` as a tool call. On the Chat Completions path that means every bare recipient. The recipient here is `assistant<|channel|>analysis`: `to=assistant` addresses the assistant, not a function, and the embedded `<|channel|>` marker ends up in the name. `_normalize_recipient` already strips a misparsed `<|constrain|>` from recipients. Handling `<|channel|>` the same way, and not treating an `assistant` recipient as a function, would probably fix this.

**Related:** #32587 reports `<|channel|>` leaking into gpt-oss tool names (for example `ls<|channel|>commentary`) in multi-turn use. This is a single-turn, parser-only repro of the same symptom, and may share a fix. #35906 sanitises recipients on the Responses API path.

Fixture: [`gpt-oss/llamacpp-stray-commentary-header`](https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall/blob/d27dceba4fdbef4981f0144eb0ae2e1766d5ffc3/fixtures/gpt-oss/imported.jsonl#L17)

I found this with an automated conformance harness. The report was drafted with AI assistance, and I verified the repro above by running it on both versions.

Found by canitoolcall (https://github.com/redd34/canitoolcall), an offline conformance suite for tool-call parsers.

title: [Bug]: minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 arg converters drop the last parameter when the model omits the closing tag (same class as #57699)
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM main (probed 2026-09-20; minimax_m2.py @ 24bfbd5d, deepseek_v4.py @ 39e33db7)
- Parser-only bug: reproduction needs no GPU, no model, no server.

### Describe the bug

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

**1. minimax_m2 - vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py `_minimax_m2_arg_converter`**

`_PARAM_RE` only ends a value at the closing parameter tag or at the next parameter open tag. The trailing `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` extraction runs only under `if partial:`, so the final conversion drops the last parameter. With `stream_arg_deltas=True`, the streamed partial conversions have already emitted the value, and the flush at tool-call end produces a shorter JSON - the same client-visible divergence as #57699.

Model output:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather">
<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>
<parameter name="unit">celsius
</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

non-streaming: `arguments == {"city": "Seattle"}` - `unit` is silently lost.

**2. glm47_moe - vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py `_glm47_arg_converter`**

`_ARG_RE` requires the value close tag; the `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` extraction is under `if partial:`. `stream_arg_deltas=True` is set. Same divergence: a tool call that omits the last closing arg_value tag yields non-streaming `arguments` without the trailing parameter.

**3. deepseek_v4 (inherited by v32/v41) - vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py `_dsml_arg_converter`**

Same `if partial:` structure. Additionally, the partial branch swallows JSON failures with `contextlib.suppress` and **drops the value entirely**, while the complete branch falls back to the literal text. So a trailing `string="false"` parameter whose partial value is not yet valid JSON is discarded even mid-stream.

### Reproduction (CPU only)

```python
from vllm.parser.minimax_m2 import _minimax_m2_arg_converter

raw = '<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>\n<parameter name="unit">celsius\n'
print(_minimax_m2_arg_converter(raw, partial=True))   # {"city": "Seattle", "unit": "celsius\n"}
print(_minimax_m2_arg_converter(raw, partial=False))  # {"city": "Seattle"}  <- unit dropped
```

Equivalent direct calls to `_glm47_arg_converter` (glm47_moe) and `_dsml_arg_converter` (deepseek_v4) show the same drop.

### Expected behavior

Mirror the qwen3 fix (#57707): the trailing-partial extraction should also run in the final conversion, so a properly closed tool call keeps its last parameter value. For deepseek_v4, the partial branch should also fall back to the literal text like the complete branch does.

I can send PRs (one per parser, following the fix shape of #57707) with regression tests mirroring TestUnclosedLastParameter in tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py.

The tool parser is inconsistent with its own streaming mode. Downstream, `messages_full_converter` (`/v1/messages` non-streaming) then never sees that text, while `message_stream_converter` emits it as a text block after the tool_use block - for the same generation, /v1/messages streaming shows the trailing text and non-streaming loses it. ### Root cause Non-streaming `extract_tool_calls` implementations truncate content at the tool-call start token and never resume afterwards: - deepseekv3_tool_parser.py: content = text before `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>` - hermes_tool_parser.py:109: `content = model_output[: model_output.find(self.tool_call_start_token)]` Streaming implementations emit post-tool text as content deltas (deepseekv3_tool_parser.py:248, `DeltaMessage(tool_calls=[], content=text)`). ### Expected behavior Both delivery modes return the same content for the same generation. ### Proposed fix Make the DeepSeek-V3 parser's non-streaming parse include the post-tool text, matching its own streaming mode. The same truncation exists in hermes_tool_parser.py and can follow separately if maintainers agree it is also unintended. OpenAI clients currently lose this text in non-streaming mode, so returning it is a correction, not a new feature. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
