title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V3/V3.1 tool parser drops the tool call when start+end tokens land in the same streaming delta
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment (CPU-only, no GPU needed to reproduce)</summary>

```text
vllm version   : 0.24.0
transformers   : (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 tokenizer loaded via AutoTokenizer)
torch          : 2.12.1+cpu
Python         : 3.10.12 (Linux)
CUDA           : not applicable, this is a pure tool-parser bug
```

</details>

###  Describe the bug

`DeepSeekV3ToolParser.extract_tool_calls_streaming` (and the near-identical `DeepSeekV31ToolParser`) silently drops a tool call whenever its start and end tokens (`<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>` / `<｜tool▁call▁end｜>`) land in the same streaming delta, instead of one token at a time.

The state machine branches purely on comparing start/end token counts between `previous_token_ids` and `current_token_ids`:

```python
# case -- we're starting a new tool call
if cur_tool_start_count > cur_tool_end_count and cur_tool_start_count > prev_tool_start_count:
    ...
# case -- the current tool call is being closed.
elif cur_tool_start_count == cur_tool_end_count and cur_tool_end_count >= prev_tool_end_count:
    if self.prev_tool_call_arr is None or len(self.prev_tool_call_arr) == 0:
        logger.debug("attempting to close tool call, but no tool call")
        return None
```
(`vllm/tool_parsers/deepseekv3_tool_parser.py`, around line 178 and line 208; same shape in `deepseekv31_tool_parser.py`.)

This assumes a tool call always spends at least one delta with `start_count > end_count` (i.e., the opening tag is observed strictly before the closing tag in a *separate* call). When a single delta instead contains a *complete* tool call — start tag, name, arguments, and end tag all at once — `cur_tool_start_count` and `cur_tool_end_count` become equal in the very first call for that tool. The code takes the "closing" branch, finds `prev_tool_call_arr` empty (nothing was ever opened), logs `"attempting to close tool call, but no tool call"`, and returns `None`. The tool call is gone — not delayed, not merged into the next delta, just dropped. `extract_tool_calls` (non-streaming) parses the exact same text correctly, so this is a streaming-only regression relative to the final output.

This isn't an exotic corner case: any time a chunk boundary batches more than one token together — a short function name/arguments, `--stream-interval > 1`, or plain scheduler batching under load — the whole call can arrive in one delta.

This is the same failure mode already fixed for DeepSeek-V3.2 in #36056 ("[Bugfix] Fix Deepseekv32 tool parser when stream interval > 1"), which replaced V3.2's incremental character-by-character state machine with a buffer-until-complete-block strategy specifically because "with stream_interval > 1, multiple parameters or closing tags can arrive in a single delta, causing the state machine to skip parameters and silently drop arguments." `deepseekv3_tool_parser.py` and `deepseekv31_tool_parser.py` still use the old per-token-assumption approach and hit the identical problem — they just never got the same fix.

### Reproduction (no GPU, real vLLM + real DeepSeek-V3 tokenizer)

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.tool_parsers.deepseekv3_tool_parser import DeepSeekV3ToolParser

tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3", trust_remote_code=True)

text = (
    '<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>'
    '<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>function<｜tool▁sep｜>get_weather\n'
    '```json\n{"x": 42}\n```<｜tool▁call▁end｜>'
    '<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>'
)

# Non-streaming: parses correctly.
final = DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok).extract_tool_calls(text, None)
print("final:", [(c.function.name, c.function.arguments) for c in final.tool_calls])
# final: [('get_weather', '{"x": 42}')]

# Streaming: the whole tool call arrives in a single delta.
token_ids = tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False)
dm = DeepSeekV3ToolParser(tok).extract_tool_calls_streaming(
    previous_text="", current_text=text, delta_text=text,
    previous_token_ids=[], current_token_ids=token_ids, delta_token_ids=token_ids,
    request=None,
)
print("streamed:", dm)
# streamed: None   <-- tool call silently dropped
```

Swapping in `DeepSeekV31ToolParser` with the V3.1-style delimiter format (`<｜tool▁sep｜>` without the ```` ```json ```` fence) reproduces the same `None`.

Character-by-character streaming (feeding the text one character at a time, as most real single-token deltas would) does *not* trigger this — it's specifically the "start and end both show up before the parser ever sees a start-only state" case that's mishandled.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [RFC]: KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters
body:
**Status:** Draft · **PRs:** #58207 (group size), #58380 (prefer `BLHNC`, stacked on #58207)

## TL;DR

Speculative drafters on hybrid models add a small KV cache bucket of their own, which breaks vLLM's KV cache grouping heuristic in two ways:

- **Too many groups (Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash):** a one-layer drafter bucket forces **one group per layer**: Qwen3.5-27B goes from 4 to 70 groups (#49730), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 4 to 46. Each group rebuilds attention metadata every step, so DFlash loses much of its speedup; forcing fewer groups today costs KV cache capacity.
- **Full attention padding (MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash):** the 5-layer drafter bucket sets the group size, which doesn't divide the target's 9 full attention layers, so a full attention padding layer is allocated for the whole context (#58175). Kimi-K3 + DSpark has the same problem: its 5-layer drafter bucket pads the 24 MLA (full attention) layers, with 20 groups.

Checked and unaffected (identical grouping with and without these PRs): GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark.

A two-part proposal fixes both:

| part | problem | fix | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 · #58207** | small drafter buckets force per-layer KV groups, or full attn padding | pick the group size by worst-case padding **bytes**; `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3) | 46 → **17** groups, **+54%** tok/s @c=1, **+36%** @c=32 | 11 → **7** groups, no full attn padding, KV capacity 5.76M → 5.96M |
| **2 · #58380** | `LBHNC` forces padding when drafter bytes/token ≠ target's | prefer `BLHNC` when the backends can run it and it avoids full attn padding or needs fewer groups | **5** groups, no padding, 7.53M tokens (> main's 7.42M); Triton only today | stays `LBHNC` at 7 groups (`BLHNC` would need 12 and has no full attn padding to remove) |

The parts are complementary: part 2 picks the path; part 1 is the fallback path (§5).

---

## 1. Background

**Motivation.** Enabling DFlash on Qwen3.5-27B raises the number of KV cache groups from 4 to **70**. Without a drafter, its 64 layers (48 GDN + 16 full attention) form 4 groups of 16; with DFlash, every layer gets its own group (64 target + 6 drafter). The drafter adds a one-layer full attention bucket, and the grouping heuristic falls back to one group per layer (#49730). Every group rebuilds its attention metadata each step, and GDN (linear attention) metadata builders are expensive, so this becomes per-step host overhead and DFlash runs well below its expected speedup; the effect is larger on Qwen3.5-4B. Forcing a larger group size recovers the throughput but, with today's grouping, costs KV cache capacity.

A drafter can also cost KV cache capacity rather than speed. MiMo-V2.5 + its DFlash drafter has buckets `[9 full, 39 SW, 5 drafter SW]`: the drafter bucket is the smallest, so the group size becomes 5, and the 9 full attention layers get a padding layer that grows with context (#58175 reports ~10% more KV capacity once it's removed). Kimi-K3 + its DSpark drafter behaves the same way (Case 3).

Related reports:

| report | model | groups | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| #49730 | Qwen3.5-27B / 4B + DFlash (H100) | 4 without DFlash → 70 with (one per layer) | DFlash ITL much slower than expected; forcing gs=16 recovers ~10% tok/s on 27B but shrinks KV capacity 216k → 141k tokens |
| #51742 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (H200) | 46 | `build_attn_metadata` ~31 ms/step vs ~6 ms at 10 groups; output tok/s ~2× at c=1 with fewer groups |
| #52297 | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | — | one GDN `build()` takes ~900 µs and is repeated per group |
| #58175 | MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash | 11 | 1 full attn padding layer; removing it gives +10.57% KV capacity (their setup); +8.4% in ours (5.76M → 6.25M) |
| this RFC | Kimi-K3 + DSpark (`RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`, TP4) | 20 | 1 MLA (full attn) padding layer; #58207: 17 groups, no MLA padding, +0.37% KV capacity |
| #42505, #46462 | Qwen3.5 / 3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash | — | DFlash slower than expected / than baseline at higher concurrency; not root-caused, likely related |

This RFC's own measurement (§4.1): Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash on B300 goes from 460 → 733 tok/s at c=1 when the 46 groups drop to 17.

### 1.0 Terms

| term | meaning |
|---|---|
| bucket | all layers whose KV cache specs merge (same attention type and shape) |
| group / `group_size` (gs) | a KV cache group shares one block table; buckets are split into groups of `group_size` layers |
| page | one layer's slice of a block; its size is that layer's bytes/token × block size |
| padding | layer slots in a group with no layer behind them; allocated but never written |
| manager vs kernel block | the KV manager allocates *manager* blocks; attention kernels may need them split into smaller *kernel* blocks |
| `LBHNC` | layer-outermost `KVCacheLayout` (today's default): every page is resized to one size, each group gets `group_size` pages per block |
| `BLHNC` | block-outermost `KVCacheLayout`: a block is one contiguous run of per-layer pages, so pages of different sizes share a block. `LBNHC`/`BLNHC` group the same way as `LBHNC`/`BLHNC` |

### 1.1 Buckets, groups, padding

```
Legend:  F/f = target/DRAFTER full attn   S/s = target/DRAFTER sliding window   M = mamba/GDN
         ▓ = full attn padding (grows with context, up to max_model_len)
         ░ = SW / mamba padding or idle page (bounded by window / state)

drafter full-attn group, group_size = 5 (one physical block):
│ f │ ▓ │ ▓ │ ▓ │ ▓ │   4 of 5 pages never written

every group's block has the same byte size (block IDs are shared across groups)
```

| cost | grows with | note |
|---|---|---|
| per-step metadata | # groups | one block table + builder call per group; GDN builders are expensive |
| KV capacity | padded slots × bytes/request | full attn slot: up to `max_model_len` tokens; SW / mamba slot: bounded |

### 1.2 Bad cases

```python
group_size = min(bucket sizes)                       # main
if max(bucket sizes) < 1.5 * min(bucket sizes):
    group_size = max(bucket sizes)
```

The heuristic sizes groups from bucket **counts** only. A drafter adds a small bucket of its own, which breaks it in the ways below. Each group is drawn as `[ ]` with one letter per layer slot.

#### Case 1: Qwen3.5 / 3.6 + DFlash: a one-layer drafter bucket forces one group per layer

Qwen3.5-27B + DFlash (4 → 70 groups), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (4 → 46), Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 (4 → 41). Per-step metadata overhead grows with the layer count.

```
Qwen3.6 alone:     buckets [30 M, 10 F]              gs = 10  →  4 groups
Qwen3.6 + DFlash:  buckets [30 M, 10 F, 5 s, 1 f]    gs = min(30, 10, 5, 1) = 1

bucket                   layers   groups on main (one layer each)
target mamba/GDN    M      30     [M][M][M][M][M][M][M][M][M][M] … [M]   30
target full attn    F      10     [F][F][F][F][F][F][F][F][F][F]         10
drafter SW          s       5     [s][s][s][s][s]                         5
drafter full attn   f       1     [f]   ← smallest bucket sets gs = 1     1
                                                                        ────
                                        metadata builds per step:        46
```

With #58207: Qwen3.6 + DFlash 17 groups, Qwen3.5 + Eagle3 9 groups.

#### Case 2: MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash: the drafter's bucket doesn't divide the target's

MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash. The 5-layer drafter bucket is the smallest, so it sets gs=5, and the 9 full attention layers get a padding slot that grows with context.

Why full attention padding is the one that matters: a padding slot costs whatever a real layer of that type would hold for each request.

| padding slot | holds per request | MiMo-V2.5, per slot |
|---|---|---|
| full attention | every token of the context | 2.5 KiB/token × 256k tokens ≈ **640 MiB** (≈ 2.5 GiB at 1M) |
| sliding window | only the window (128 tokens), plus tokens in flight | 5 KiB/token × 128 ≈ **0.6 MiB** (≈ 41 MiB worst case with 8k in-flight tokens) |

So one full attention padding slot wastes as much as hundreds of sliding-window slots, and it keeps growing with context length.

```
main    gs = 5 → 11 groups
  F  [FFFFF][FFFF▓]              ← full attn padding
  S  [SSSSS] ×7 + [SSSS░]
  s  [sssss]

#58207  gs = 9 → 7 groups
  F  [FFFFFFFFF]                 ← no full attn padding
  S  [SSSSSSSS░] ×4 + [SSSSSSS░░]
  s  [sssss░░░░]
```

#### Case 3: Kimi-K3 + DSpark: same as Case 2, with MLA

Kimi-K3 has 69 KDA (linear attention) and 24 MLA (full attention) layers; the DSpark drafter (`RedHatAI/Kimi-K3-speculator.dspark`) adds 5 sliding-window layers. The drafter bucket sets gs=5, which doesn't divide 24, so an MLA padding slot is allocated for the whole context.

```
L = KDA (linear attention)

main    gs = 5 → 20 groups
  L  [LLLLL] ×13 + [LLLL░]
  F  [FFFFF] ×4 + [FFFF▓]        ← MLA (full attn) padding
  s  [sssss]

#58207  gs = 6 → 17 groups
  L  [LLLLLL] ×9 + [LLLLL░] ×3
  F  [FFFFFF] ×4                 ← no MLA padding
  s  [sssss░]
```

Served (Kimi-K3-pruned75, same 93 layers, TP4): KV capacity 4.76M → 4.78M tokens at 131k context. #58380 keeps `LBNHC` here.

---

## 2. Part 1 · #58207: group size by worst-case padding bytes

Replace the [min / 1.5×-max heuristic](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/b3a87b2d04e6439e2a1aef0cbf9ca65328076c86/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L1547-L1558) with a search over group sizes that minimizes **worst-case padding bytes** per request, bounded below so groups can't explode:

```python
lo = max(smallest bucket, min(min_kv_cache_group_layers, largest bucket))
group_size = argmin over gs in [lo, largest bucket] of
    (Σ padding_slots(bucket, gs) × spec.max_memory_usage_bytes(vllm_config), num_groups(gs))
```

Padding is costed in bytes, so full attention padding (which grows with `max_model_len`) is avoided in favor of bounded sliding-window / mamba padding. The lower bound keeps groups from exploding: never below the smallest bucket, and never below `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3), so a one-layer drafter bucket can't force one group per layer.

```
Qwen3.6 + DFlash, gs = 3 → 17 groups (each bucket padded independently)
  M  [MMM] ×10    F  [FFF][FFF][FF▓][FF▓]    s  [sss][ss░]    f  [f▓▓]
```

## 3. Part 2 · #58380: prefer `BLHNC`

In `BLHNC` a block is one contiguous run of per-layer pages, so pages of different sizes share a block instead of being padded to one size. The widest non-state bucket sets the block; mamba / SW groups split to fit it. #58380 prefers these layouts when specs have mixed page sizes **and** every backend runs each attention block unsplit, since packed blocks can't be split into smaller kernel blocks:

| backend (B300) | kernel block sizes | can use `BLHNC` |
|---|---|---|
| Triton | any multiple of 16 | yes |
| FlashInfer | 16 / 32 / 64 | no |
| FlashAttention hd256 (FA4) | 128 | no |

**`BLHNC` cost check:** `BLHNC` is not always better (MiMo below: 7 → 12 groups), so #58380 also computes both groupings from the specs and picks `BLHNC` only if the `LBHNC` grouping would pad full attention, or `BLHNC` needs fewer groups.

Each row below is a separate group; rows align because every block is the same size:

```
Qwen3.6 + DFlash: 5 groups, 12-page blocks
full-attn ×1   │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │   f   │   10 target + drafter (2 pages): no padding
mamba ×3       │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ M │ ░ │ ░ │   10 GDN states each, 2 idle pages
drafter sw ×1  │   s   │   s   │   s   │   s   │   s   │ ░ │ ░ │   5 layers × 2 pages, 2 idle pages

MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash under `BLHNC` (not picked by the cost check): 12 groups, 9-page blocks
full-attn ×1   │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │ F │   9 full pages: no padding
SWA ×10        │   S   │   S   │   S   │   S   │ ░ │   4 layers × 2 pages, 1 idle page (one group has 3)
drafter SW ×1  │  d d d d d  (1.6 pages each)  │ ░ │   5 layers × 64 KiB = 8 pages, 1 idle page
```

## 4. Results by model and layout

### 4.1 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash (1× B300)

| plan | groups | padding / request @256k | KV capacity | tok/s c=1 / c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 46 | 0 | 7.42M | 460 / 4654 |
| #58207 | 17 | 3.05 GiB (full attn) | 5.19M | 733 / 6495 |
| **#58380** (Triton, `BLHNC`) | **5** | **58 MiB** | **7.53M** | **746 / 7463** |

### 4.2 MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash (TP2)

| plan | groups | padding / request @256k | KV capacity |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 11 | 726 MiB (incl. 1 full attn layer) | 5.76M |
| #58175 | 18 | **90 MiB** | **6.25M** |
| #58207 | **7** | 469 MiB | 5.96M |
| `BLHNC` (#58380 doesn't pick it) | 12 | 266 MiB | 6.10M |

Padding is worst case (8192 in-flight tokens). Full attn padding grows with context, so `BLHNC` wins outright for Qwen3.6; MiMo has none, so it's a trade between groups and bounded bytes.

### 4.3 Qwen3.6 + DFlash: `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` sweep

![min-kv-cache-group-layers sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/af4013a3827d250b266c6e48b1fc124880523780/pareto_min_layers.png)

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV capacity | padding/req @256k | c=1 | c=32 | with #52297 ² c=1 / c=32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M | 0 | 460 | 4654 | 653 / 5735 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M | 1.02 GiB (+17%) | 684 | 5711 | 716 / 6247 |
| **3 (default)** | 3 | 17 | 5.19M | 3.02 GiB (+50%) | 710 | 6339 | 727 / 7100 |
| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M | 4 GiB (+67%) | 726 | 6676 | 758 / 6865 |

² #52297 (open PR) computes GDN attention metadata once per step instead of per group, making extra groups cheaper.

### 4.4 Qwen3.6 + DFlash: `BLHNC` vs `LBHNC`

![BLHNC vs LBHNC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/f52d0d4bb0b941fff5dbc5834f62d865db084188/pareto_packed.png)

## 5. How the two parts fit together

**Defaults after both PRs merge** (default backends, no `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT`). Padding is per request at 256k context (worst case, 8192 in-flight tokens):

| model (B300 backend) | main today | after #58207 + #58380 |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6 + DFlash (FlashInfer/FA) | `LBHNC`, 46 groups, no padding | `LBHNC`, **17** groups, 3.05 GiB padding (full attn) |
| Qwen3.6 + DFlash (`--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`) | `LBHNC`, 46 groups, no padding | **`BLHNC`, 5** groups, 58 MiB padding |
| MiMo-V2.5 + DFlash (FA) | `LBHNC`, 11 groups, 726 MiB padding (640 MiB full attn) | `LBHNC`, **7** groups, 469 MiB padding (no full attn) |
| Kimi-K3 + DSpark (TP4) | `LBHNC`, 20 groups, 1 MLA padding layer | `LBHNC`, **17** groups, no MLA padding |
| MiMo-V2.6 + MTP (FA) | `LBHNC`, 6 groups, 203 MiB padding (SW) | unchanged |
| Qwen3.5 + Eagle3 (FlashInfer/FA) | `LBHNC`, 41 groups, no padding | `LBHNC`, 9 groups, 4 drafter full attn padding slots |
| GLM-5.3-Flash + DFlash2, MiniMax-M3 + DSpark, DeepSeek-V4-Flash + DSpark | unchanged | unchanged |
| single page size (Gemma3, gpt-oss, Llama4, Qwen3.5, …) | unchanged | unchanged |

**Recommendation:** land #58207 first (helps every layout/backend), then #58380. `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` / connector preferences still win.

---

## 6. Alternatives considered

Other open PRs that change this heuristic, and what each gives for Qwen3.6 + DFlash:

| PR | approach | Qwen3.6 + DFlash | shortcoming |
|---|---|---|---|
| #51742 | ignore one-layer buckets when taking the min | gs=5, 10 groups | pads the drafter's full attn layer with 4 slots that grow with context |
| #58175 | shrink gs to a divisor of the full attn bucket sizes (targets MiMo) | gs=1, 46 groups | doesn't help drafters |
| #49472 | minimize padding + number of groups, counted in layers | gs=5, 10 groups | a padded full attn layer counts the same as a sliding-window one, so it pads full attn |

Other approaches:

- **Bigger `block_size` for the lone drafter group** (same bytes, fewer layers): prefix-cache hits align to the LCM of group block sizes, so hits get ~5× coarser for every group.
- **Only forbid one layer per group (`group_size ≥ 2`) and minimize padding:** still 24 groups for Qwen3.6 + DFlash, and over-splits models with cheap padding (Gemma3-27B 7 → 31 groups).
- **Absolute cap on the number of groups:** the right cap depends on the backend (GDN vs FlashAttention metadata cost).
- **Drafter-aware sizing** (size groups from target buckets, pad the drafter): worst case when the drafter has a full attention layer, and drafter layers can only be identified heuristically at grouping time.
- **Separate KV pool for drafter layers:** removes the constraint entirely, but is a much larger allocator change.
- **#58345 (rescale sliding-window blocks for `BLHNC`):** on main (since #53007) sliding-window layers already use the full attention block size when the backend allows it (group block sizes 262144 ×3, 592, 592); when it doesn't, rescaling would need kernel-block splitting, which `BLHNC` can't do.

---

## 7. Open questions

1. **Default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers`:** 3 (17 groups, −30% KV capacity on Qwen3.6 + DFlash) or 4 (10 groups, +2–5% tok/s, −35%)? Should it depend on whether the model has GDN layers?
2. **`BLHNC` with FlashInfer / FlashAttention:** re-page inside the kernels (as #55219 / #57169 do for sparse MLA), or stop inflating the block size for block-outermost layouts (but then few GDN states fit per block)?
3. **FlashAttention drafter block size:** the 128-only FA4 hd256 kernel block is derived from the *target's* head size and applied to a hd128 drafter, causing `No common block size for 592` on main unless `--block-size 128` is set. Fixed separately by #58630.
4. **Validation:** #58380 switches mixed-page-size models to `BLHNC` when the cost check passes on capable backends; needs accuracy and throughput validation beyond DFlash and MiMo.

---

## 8. Methodology

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 [--min-kv-cache-group-layers N] \
  [--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN] \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

| item | value |
|---|---|
| hardware | 1× B300 per run (MiMo: TP2, `max_model_len` 1M) |
| runs | single; noise ~2–3% (repeated gs=5) |
| interactivity | 1000 / p99 TPOT |
| acceptance length | 5.1–5.2 in all Qwen runs |
| `--block-size 128` | needed on all variants, including main: FlashAttention's 128-only FA4 hd256 kernel block is derived from the target's head size and also applied to the hd128 drafter, which otherwise fails with `No common block size for 592` |


---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to run the experiments and draft this RFC; I have reviewed its contents.

title: [Tracking][Spec Decode] Adaptive DSpark Bring-Up Tracker
body: Tracking issue to organize the adaptive verification support for DSpark speculative decoding ## Backend Support Adaptive verification has a firm requirement that the attention backend must not use the CPU-side query lengths as a source-of-truth, instead using the gpu tensors (so that we can run the confidence-based assignment on the GPU without synchronizing the CPU). Additionally, kernels must be able to support decode batches where requests have different query lengths per request. Currently, the following backends are known to support variable lengths: - FLASH_ATTN - DSV4 Attention **TODO**: - Hybrid / Linear attention (requires significant effort) - - Mamba (for NVIDIA Nemotron models) - - GDN (for Qwen3.x models) - - Kimi KDA (for Kimi K3) - DSV3-style MLA - FlashInfer GQA: - - TRTLLM kernel support exists, just needs to be plugged into vLLM. Minor change. - - CUTLASS backend of FlashInfer may need additional support to avoid the cpu query lengths ## Online Profiling The initial version does profiling at startup to estimate the verification step time by replaying the recorded CUDA graphs. This is known to have some drift: We want to extend this to fully online profiling in the future. However, there are some challenges that make this tricky: - Online profiling may lead to "dead spots": one-time latency spikes make a certain batch size appear unattractive, leading to the adaptive verifier to never select that batch size, which leads to negative feedback and stale data limiting our range of profiled values. Generally there is an "exploration vs exploitation" problem here, as well as a requirement for some way to detect and eliminate outliers (such as those caused by JIT compilation) - Variable sequence lengths make it hard to measure a single reliable estimate of execution time for a given number of tokens. In practice we will want some way to account for this: either tracking measured points in 2D (num_tokens, max_seq_len or mean_seq_len), or estimating the overhead added per-token of KV reads ## Tuning Confidence Scores The confidence scores are not always perfectly calibrated. In particular, it seems like the deeper positions have higher variance and some bias in their expectation. The DSpark paper suggests [Sequential Temperature Scaling (STS)](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.05147v1) as an online solution to calibrating these estimates. I did not see much benefit when adding this feature, but we should experiment more thoroughly and assess the potential benefit of improved confidence estimates. Here are the results from one run with DSV4-Flash-0731: ## First-Class Observability ### Exposing Timings and Adaptive-SD Metrics Now that we are profiling different phases of the worker execution (model runner, proposer), and tracking the step time by batch size, we will want to expose these to the user for observability. This will help with performance tuning and development, as well as for monitoring of production deployments at scale. We will want to propagate the metrics to both the prometheus / frontend, as well as to the iteration-level logging feature. We will also want some way to report our other metrics for adaptive verification: confidence success rate (mismatch between "expected" AL and "achieved" AL), performance model reliability (difference between "expected" step time and "actual" step time), etc. ### Benchmarking Compatibility Adaptive speculative decoding will change what it means for speculative decoding to have high acceptance rate. AL is no longer a "golden" metric for success. As a start, this PR enables detailed, per-request and per-step speculative decoding metrics to be exposed in the OpenAI response. This can be used to report exact speculative decoding statistics and aggregated on the client to fit the use-case. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48915 ## Feature Compatibility - [ ] Logprob extraction support ([see here](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47808#discussion_r3723768178))

title: [Bug]: [ROCm] DeepSeek-V4 sparse indexer is a dead end on non-MI3xx GPUs, though working torch fallbacks exist in-tree
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Abridged environment (key versions; 2-node cluster)</summary>

```text
vLLM:    0.26.1.dev0+g568afb3a1.d20260808
PyTorch: 2.12.0+rocm7.14.0
Python:  3.14.4
ROCm:    7.14, RCCL 2.30.4
GPU:     2x AMD Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo APU, gfx1151), 1 GPU per node
Nodes:   2-node Ray cluster, TP=2, Thunderbolt interconnect (RCCL NET/Socket)
Model:   DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (quantization=deepseek_v4_fp8, fp8_ds_mla KV cache)
AITER:   built from source (ROCm/aiter @ main, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1151); imports and JITs fine
```

Serve command:

```bash
vllm serve /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --distributed-executor-backend ray
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Three interacting gates currently make DeepSeek-V4 (and presumably any model using the DSA sparse indexer with `fp8_ds_mla`) impossible to run on ROCm GPUs other than MI3xx — while torch reference fallbacks for exactly this situation already exist in-tree, are wired with correct arguments, and work when made reachable (verified on a 2× gfx1151 cluster, now serving).

**Gate 1 — the indexer requires AITER.** During the profiling forward pass, `sparse_attn_indexer.py::forward_hip` raises:

```
Sparse attention indexer ROCm path is only supported on AITER.
Please enable aiter with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
```

**Gate 2 — the advice in that error cannot work.** `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` is silently ignored on non-MI3xx because `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` hard-gates on platform:

```python
def is_aiter_found_and_supported() -> bool:
    ...
    if current_platform.is_rocm() and IS_AITER_FOUND:
        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx
        return on_mi3xx()
    return False
```

So the user is sent in a loop: the error demands an env var that the platform gate then discards, even with AITER installed and importable.

**Gate 3 — the in-tree fallbacks are unreachable.** `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` contains `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` and `fp8_mqa_logits_torch`, and both dispatchers (`rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) already call them in their `else` branches when the AITER Triton module is unavailable. But reaching the dispatchers requires AITER enabled (gates 1–2), and with AITER enabled the module lookup always succeeds, so the AITER Triton kernels are always selected.

On RDNA3/3.5 those AITER Triton kernels cannot compile regardless (no fp8 WMMA), so whitelisting the arch in gate 2 just moves the failure into Triton:

```
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError
  o = tl.dot(q, k.T)
      ^
Unsupported lhs dtype fp8e4nv
(aiter/ops/triton/attention/pa_mqa_logits.py, deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1)
```

i.e. every path on this hardware terminates in an error one step before working fallback code.

### Reproduction

1. 2× gfx1151, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, serve command in the environment section → gate 1 error.
2. Add `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` → identical error (gate 2).
3. Whitelist gfx1151 in `is_aiter_found_and_supported()` → Triton `fp8e4nv` CompilationError in the AITER paged-MQA kernel (gate 3).

### Tested fix (cluster is serving with this)

**a) `vllm/_aiter_ops.py`** — accept gfx1151 as AITER-capable:

```diff
-        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx
-
-        return on_mi3xx()
+        from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_mi3xx, on_gfx1151
+
+        return on_mi3xx() or on_gfx1151()
```

**b) `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`** — skip the AITER Triton module lookup on gfx1151 so the existing torch fallbacks run (same change in both dispatchers):

```diff
-    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled():
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151
+
+    # gfx1151: Triton cannot compile tl.dot with fp8e4nv inputs; skip the
+    # AITER Triton kernels so the torch reference fallback below is used.
+    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151():
         aiter_paged_mqa_logits_module = paged_mqa_logits_module()
```

```diff
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx1151
+
     aiter_mqa_logits_module = None
-    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled():
+    if rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() and not on_gfx1151():
         aiter_mqa_logits_module = mqa_logits_module()
```

The prefill dispatcher (`rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`) needs the same gate: its AITER kernel performs the same fp8 `tl.dot` and fails identically on the first real prefill if only the paged path is patched.

A cleaner resolution than piling onto the arch whitelist is probably per-kernel capability gating: dispatchers select the AITER Triton kernel only on archs where it is known to compile (mi3xx / gfx942 / gfx950 — the gfx942 special case already exists in `rocm_fp8_mqa_logits`), else torch fallback — and gate 1's error message should not recommend an env var that gate 2 ignores. Happy to turn this into a PR if maintainers agree on the preferred shape.

Note: the sparse-attention Triton kernels in the same file are unaffected — they dequantize fp8→bf16 in-kernel before `tl.dot` and compile fine on gfx1151.

### Secondary finding: torch fallback vs FULL cudagraph capture

Once reachable, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch` is not capture-safe (`.item()` / data-dependent host loops), but `@eager_break_during_capture` intentionally runs ops inline when `forward_context.cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.FULL` (`compilation/breakable_cudagraph.py`), so FULL capture crashes:

```
File ".../rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py", line 290, in fp8_paged_mqa_logits_torch
    seq_len = int(context_lens[i].item())
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing
(hipErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported)
```

If the fallbacks become officially reachable, the op should be treated as non-capturable when the torch path is active (or cudagraph disabled for it). We run with `--enforce-eager` (also required on this cluster: piecewise capture deadlocked in RCCL NET/Socket collectives; related to #32180).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: MFU/MBU bills linear-attention layers of hybrid models as full attention; reported bandwidth exceeds the GPU's peak
body:
### Your current environment

RTX 4090 24 GB (spec 1,008 GB/s; memory clock 10,501 MHz per `nvidia-smi -q`), driver 590.48.01 (CUDA 13.1), Ubuntu 24.04, vLLM `0.30.1rc1.dev80+g26f49e336` (nightly cu130 wheel), torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.17.0. The rented machine is gone, so I do not have `collect_env.py` output; `vllm/v1/metrics/` is unchanged between `26f49e336` and current `main` (`8b84e150`, 2026-09-24).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`AttentionMetrics` bills full attention (QKV/O weights, KV-cache reads, attention FLOPs) for every one of `num_hidden_layers`. Hybrid models with linear-attention layers only have full attention in a fraction of them: Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next use 3 Gated DeltaNet layers for every full-attention layer (`layer_types`, `full_attention_interval: 4`). #55624 handles sliding-window/full alternation but not linear-attention or Mamba layers, so the reported MBU for these models is not physically possible.

Config-only check (no GPU):

```python
from tests.v1.metrics.test_perf_metrics import create_mock_vllm_config
from vllm.transformers_utils.config import get_config
from vllm.v1.metrics.perf import ModelMetrics

mm = ModelMetrics(create_mock_vllm_config(get_config("Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", trust_remote_code=False)))
print({m.component_type(): getattr(m, "num_hidden_layers", None) for m in mm.metrics})
# {'attn': 32, 'ffn': 32, 'unembed': None}; layer_types has 8 "full_attention" and 24 "linear_attention"
```

Measured with `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-mfu-metrics` (`VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=2`) and `vllm bench serve` (random prompts, 512 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 3 × batch requests per cell). The table only uses 2-second log intervals inside the benchmark's wall time that have no prefill in them (`Avg prompt throughput: 0.0`), so it is pure decode:

| batch × context | reported GB/s, median (run 1 / run 2) | intervals above 1,008 GB/s | same cells, layer count corrected (see below) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 × 8k | 1,164 / 1,165 | 8/8, 8/8 | 602, 0/9 above |
| 8 × 16k | 1,538 / 1,536 | 10/10, 11/11 | 652, 0/11 above |
| 32 × 8k | 1,821 / 1,831 | 10/10, 10/10 | 645, 0/13 above |

- A device-to-device copy on the same card reaches 918 GB/s (read + write, 3 trials), so the reported numbers are not physically possible.
- Control: Qwen3-4B (dense, same size, same script, same machine) never exceeds the peak: 0 of 32 decode intervals, max 881 GB/s.
- Intervention: counting only the 8 full-attention layers (a small parser reading `layer_types` / `layers_block_type`) removes every over-peak interval on the same cells.

The corrected column is not the right answer either. Dropping the 24 linear-attention layers from attention without billing them as anything leaves out their weights (1,011 M parameters for Qwen3.5-4B, counted from the safetensors headers) and their recurrent state, so the estimate becomes about 0.75× of the bytes actually moved. A correct fix needs a linear-attention component: weights, the per-request recurrent and conv state read and written every step, and nothing that grows with context. Hand accounting of what the model actually reads shows the current code over-bills bytes per decode step by about 1.43× at 8 × 8k and about 2× at 32 × 8k, and under-bills slightly at 1 × 1k.

A smaller related gap: the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next attention has an output gate (`attn_output_gate: true`; `q_proj` is `[8192, 2560]`, twice the query width), which `qkv_weight` / `qkv_proj` do not include.

Limits of this report: one GPU and one hybrid model measured; Qwen3-Next, Jamba, Falcon-H1 only checked at config level. `ncu` DRAM counters were not available in the container, so "bytes actually moved" comes from the parameter and state accounting above, not a hardware counter.

Not a duplicate as far as I can tell: no open or closed issue or PR covers MFU/MBU for linear-attention or Mamba layers (searched 2026-09-25). The two open PRs touching `perf.py` (#55474, #54228) do not touch layer counting.

I'd like to work on the fix (linear-attention component plus layer-type parsing, with tests) if that direction sounds right to the maintainers of this area.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write the scripts, drive the measurements on my rented GPU and draft this report. I reviewed the logs and the results.

title: [Perf]: turboquant_k8v4 decode penalty scales with context length (-2.8% at 3k, -31% at 55k) on Ampere SM86, no speculative decoding
body:
### Summary

On a hybrid GDN + full-attention model, `--kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4` costs almost nothing at short context but roughly a third of decode throughput at 55k prompt tokens, compared to `fp8_e4m3` with everything else identical. Speculative decoding is **off** in both arms, so this is separate from #53180 / #52475 / #53406 / #53410.

The KV-cache saving is real and large (+37% pool on the same GPUs), but on our hardware the throughput loss lands exactly on the long-context requests the bigger pool is meant to serve, which makes the feature unusable for us today.

### Environment

- vLLM **0.27.1**, stock (pip, no local patches)
- 2x RTX 3090 (**Ampere, SM 8.6**), TP=2, 250 W each
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B, hybrid GDN + full attention, own mixed W8/W4 GPTQ weight quant, `dtype=bfloat16`
  - 64 layers, `full_attention_interval=4` -> 16 full-attention layers (engine log: `TQ hybrid: full-attention layers [3, 7, 11, ..., 63]`)
  - `head_dim=256`, 24 query heads / 4 KV heads (**GQA group size 6**)

### Reproduction

Two servers, launched from the same script; the **only** difference in `non-default args` is `kv_cache_dtype`. Both without `speculative_config`.

```
vllm serve <model> \
  --dtype bfloat16 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --max-model-len 156000 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \
  --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_k8v4 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 16 \
  --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --long-prefill-token-threshold 2048 --enable-chunked-prefill
```

Arm C is the same line with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`.

Load: single stream, no concurrency, warm (same prompt run twice back to back), 800 output tokens per run, server-side sampling override (`temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, presence_penalty=1.0`). Two prompt sizes: **3,216** and **55,344** prompt tokens.

### Measurements

| | `fp8_e4m3` | `turboquant_k8v4` | delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| KV cache pool (engine log) | 357,622 tokens | 491,111 tokens | **+37.3%** |
| Max concurrency @156k | 2.29x | 3.15x | |
| Decode, 3,216 prompt tokens | 53.33 / 53.32 t/s | 51.83 / 51.82 t/s | **-2.8%** |
| Decode, 55,344 prompt tokens | 50.18 / 50.20 t/s | 34.58 / 34.58 t/s | **-31.1%** |

(Two runs per cell, both listed; run-to-run spread is <0.1 t/s.)

Engine log lines:

```
GPU KV cache size: 357,622 tokens | Maximum concurrency for 156,000 tokens per request: 2.29x   # fp8_e4m3
GPU KV cache size: 491,111 tokens | Maximum concurrency for 156,000 tokens per request: 3.15x   # turboquant_k8v4
```

Secondary observation (same runs, not isolated from prefix-cache state, so weaker evidence): TTFT on the warm 55k prompt was 1.05 s with TurboQuant vs 0.56 s with fp8, and 0.69 s vs 0.09 s on the warm 3k prompt.

Output quality with TurboQuant and no speculative decoding was clean: 0 degenerate responses across 8 probes plus a 42-item internal eval run.

### What we think is happening

The penalty is near-zero at 3k and ~31% at 55k, i.e. it tracks the number of quantized KV positions read back per decode step rather than a fixed per-step overhead. That is consistent with the dequant/rotation work sitting in the per-position read path of the Triton decode kernel, but we have not profiled it — this is an observation, not a diagnosis.

### Questions

1. Is a context-length-scaling decode penalty of this size expected for the current Triton decode kernels, or does it indicate a missed fast path for this geometry?
2. Our config (`k8v4`, GQA group size 6, `head_dim` 256) falls outside the dispatch gates of #53060 (K4V4-NC only) and #48235 (GQA group size 4). #40792 targets exactly `k8v4` GQA grouping and reports +16.5–27.2% on A100/H100 — would it be expected to change the *slope* here, or only the constant?
3. #40069 lists "CUDA/cutedsl kernels to replace the triton kernels" under Performance. Is that the tracking item for this, and is there a benchmark shape you would like measured on SM86? We can run more points on this hardware.

### Expected

Either the decode penalty stays roughly constant with context length, or the context-scaling behaviour is documented so the compression/throughput trade-off can be evaluated before deployment.

*This issue was researched and written by Ren, an AI agent operated by karls0r, with his review.*

title: [Bug][Perf][DSpark] #54674 stacked context WKV regresses TTFT ~3.3% on 2-node DGX Spark (GB10, TP=2), with no decode gain
body:
## Summary

[#54674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54674) ("[Perf][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V4 context WKV projections", merged 2026-09-17) is a **TTFT regression of ~3.2-3.3%** on 2-node DGX Spark (GB10 / SM121, TP=2) serving DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 NVFP4. It also costs ~1.5% of the KV pool. We measured no compensating decode or acceptance-rate gain.

Since the PR targets the context/prefill path, a TTFT regression is the opposite of its intended effect, so we are reporting it rather than just dropping the patch locally.

## Why the usual A/B is not enough here, and what we did instead

Throughput metrics on this platform have a large boot-to-boot spread, so a single A-vs-B comparison cannot resolve a few percent. We ran **A-B-A** (three full engine restarts) and used the two A runs to calibrate the noise floor:

| metric | A1 (without #54674) | B (with #54674) | A2 (without #54674) | A1↔A2 spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| greedy 32K decode tok/s | 65.62 | 64.57 | 60.92 | **7.2%** |
| temp0.6 8K decode tok/s (mean of 3) | 61.54 | 65.70 | 65.23 | **6.0%** |
| temp0.6 acceptance rate | 0.6539 | 0.7016 | 0.6961 | **6.5%** |
| **TTFT 8K (s)** | **2.502** | **2.589** | **2.512** | **0.4%** |
| **TTFT 32K (s)** | **10.191** | **10.551** | **10.221** | **0.3%** |

Decode throughput and DSpark acceptance rate swing 6-7% between two boots of the *same* build, so every apparent "gain" for B in those rows is inside the noise band. TTFT, by contrast, is stable to 0.3-0.4% across the two A runs — and B is consistently **+3.2%** (8K) and **+3.3%** (32K) relative to the A mean, which is roughly an order of magnitude outside that spread.

A 128K-prefill probe agrees in direction: 62.6 s with the patch vs 61.9 / 62.1 s without.

Secondary cost: GPU KV cache pool drops from **1,655,061** to **1,630,430** tokens (-1.5%), and reported max concurrency at 1M context from 1.58x to 1.55x.

## Hypothesis

With `--max-num-seqs 6` on a 2-node TP=2 GB10 pair, the stacked WKV projection does not have enough concurrent context work to amortize its extra setup, so the stacking overhead lands directly on TTFT. Configurations with larger batch or more GPUs may still benefit — we are not claiming the PR is wrong in general, only that it is a net loss in this shape.

## Reproduction

Serve command (2 nodes, one GB10 each, RoCE):

```
vllm serve nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-NVFP4 \
  --revision f1caa71142bd0be02f728c79f75042ac1e461579 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --trust-remote-code --max-num-seqs 6 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 1048576 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --block-size 256 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --quantization deepseek_v4_fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.825 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","disable_eagle_block_drop":true}' \
  --no-async-scheduling --enable-flashinfer-autotune
```

Measure TTFT at 8K and 32K prompt with 384 output tokens, greedy. **Restart the engine between arms and run A-B-A**; a single A/B will not separate a 3% TTFT effect from the decode noise if you look at throughput, and will look like a *win* if you look at `temp0.6` decode or acceptance rate.

## Environment

- 2x DGX Spark (GB10, SM121, 48 SMs, driver 580.173.02), TP=2 over RoCE, unified 128 GB/node
- vLLM nightly `2671fedf` + the merged `#54674` diff applied as a source overlay (byte-identical to the merged version apart from the `diff --git`/`index` headers)
- flashinfer 0.6.18.post1 with the #4802 SM120 sparse-MLA sources overlaid (+#5048, +#5097)
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 NVFP4, `fp8_ds_mla` KV, DSpark k=5
- Benchmarks run on an idle cluster with periodic synthetic load disabled

Happy to re-run with different `--max-num-seqs` or on a larger batch shape if that would help locate the crossover.

title: Speculative-decoding draft model (EAGLE/MTP head) compile cache key flips between two values with byte-identical startup args — shared `VllmConfig` mutated in-place during main-model full-compile startup (v0.27.1; deterministic on 0.29)
body:
## Summary

On vLLM 0.27.1 with speculative decoding (MTP head, k=1), the **draft model's** torch.compile cache identity deterministically flips between exactly two values across restarts with **byte-identical argv and environment**. The flip factor is not the command line — it is whether the **main model compiles (cold start) or loads from cache (warm start)** on that startup.

Forensics on `cache_key_factors.json` (which records the actual hash factors) show the draft's `config_hash` differs between the two generations while env/compiler factors are identical: the shared `VllmConfig` object is **mutated in-place during the main model's warmup/CUDA-graph-capture phase**, after the backbone compiles with a clean hash but before the eagle head compiles. On a 0.29 development build (commit `g38537331d`, the same build referenced in #58653) the same forensics show `eagle_head config_hash == backbone config_hash` in **9/9 compile-era startups** across two independent deployments — i.e. 0.29 appears immune.

## Environment

- vLLM **0.27.1** (stable release), single GPU, single rank
- Model: Qwen3.8-27B (W4A16 quantized), hybrid attention (linear/GDN + full), MTP module
- Speculative decoding: MTP k=1; CUDA graph `PIECEWISE`; fp8 KV cache
- 0.27.1 evidence from deployment A; 0.29 control (dev build `g38537331d`, 2026-09-19) from deployment A's current build and deployment B

## Symptom

- The draft model's AOT/compile cache directory alternates between two values (`40a960c…` ↔ `81aa37e7…`) across **17 same-signature restarts** observed during one incident window, all with identical startup args.
- Every flip costs a full draft recompile (~196 s) at the next startup whose expected generation doesn't match — the draft cache hit rate is determined by the *previous startup's shape*, not by config.

## Forensics: `cache_key_factors.json`

vLLM writes `torch_compile_cache/<short_hash>/rank_0_0/<backbone|eagle_head>/cache_key_factors.json` recording the real hash factors. Comparing the **eagle head** across the two generations:

| factor | generation 1 (main compiled) | generation 2 (main loaded) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| env_hash (231 keys) | `2e9cfbbedb14f457` | same | SAME |
| compiler_hash | `8e33489fd9` | same | SAME |
| **config_hash** | **`06b5820a50`** | **`b398c1fc03`** | **DIFF — the flip factor** |
| code_hash | `2b706e49…` | `91b0ecb5…` | DIFF (dynamo compile-counter side effect) |

Key observation: in generation 2 (clean), the eagle head's `config_hash` **equals the backbone's** (`b398c1fc03`) — the draft derives from the main config without changing hash factors. In generation 1, eagle ≠ backbone for the same process, i.e. between the backbone's compile and the eagle's compile, **something changed the config that feeds `compute_hash()`**.

## Why "same cache dir, diverging jsons"

- `compilation/backends.py:1053` (0.27.1): `if not self.compilation_config.cache_dir:` — the **shared** `CompilationConfig.cache_dir` is set by the backbone's compile; the eagle head then **reuses the backbone's cache dir** instead of deriving its own from its (now-dirty) factors.
- But each `cache_key_factors.json`'s `config_hash` is recomputed fresh at `__call__` entry (`backends.py:1034`, no caching).
- Result: both roles land in one directory while their jsons record diverging config hashes — the forensic signature that led us here.

## Startup-shape bisection (timeline, UTC)

| startup | main model | warmup+capture window | eagle config_hash | draft AOT saved as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-17 00:09–00:12 | full compile | **present, 67.6 s** | `06b5820a50` (dirty) | `81aa37e7` |
| 2026-09-17 00:37 | direct load | absent | `b398c1fc03` (clean) | `40a960c` |
| 2026-09-20 04:09 | full compile | present | dirty | `81aa37e7` |
| 2026-09-22 19:35 | direct load | absent | clean | `40a960c` |

The warmup+capture phase exists **only** on full-compile startups, and it runs **between** backbone compile and eagle compile — exactly where the mutation must occur. **Flip factor = whether the main model compiles on that startup.**

## Mechanism chain

1. Backbone `__call__` computes `config_hash` fresh (clean).
2. Main-model warmup + CUDA-graph capture runs (full-compile startups only) — **this phase mutates the shared `VllmConfig` in-place** (exact field not yet isolated).
3. Eagle head `__call__` recomputes `config_hash` from the now-mutated config → different value.
4. Draft AOT save dir (derived from `[env_hash, config_hash, code_hash, compiler_hash]`) flips; the torch_compile_cache dir does not (reuse) → diverging-jsons signature.

## Ruled out (all with file:line in 0.27.1)

- `traced_files` / `cache_dir` / `local_cache_dir`: in `CompilationConfig` ignored_factors (`compilation/config.py:792-800`)
- `num_gpu_blocks` / `num_gpu_blocks_override`: in `CacheConfig` ignored_factors
- `cudagraph_mode`: byte-identical CUDAGraphMode traces in both generations' draft AOT pickles (both `PIECEWISE`); the resolve-time downgrade warning fires **after** each draft compile in both startups
- `adjust_cudagraph_sizes_for_spec_decode`: write-back happens at `resolve()`, outside the window
- Engine-phase speculative-config mutation: `SpeculativeConfig.compute_hash` for MTP is constant `[False]`; `update_arch_*` all in `__post_init__` (construction time, identical both generations)
- `CudaGraphManager` internals (`cudagraph_utils.py:122`): own attributes, no config write points
- "0.29 caches the hash" hypothesis: 0.29's `backends.py` computes `config_hash` fresh, code isomorphic to 0.27.1 — immunity is behavioral, not a caching change

## Cross-version control (0.29 immune)

- Deployment B (0.29 dev build `g38537331d`): **9/9** compile-era startups have `eagle_head config_hash == backbone config_hash` (json forensics, same method).
- Deployment A's 0.29 build: two generations (2026-09-23, 2026-09-24 windows), likewise `backbone == draft config_hash`.
- ⇒ On 0.29 the in-window mutation either no longer happens or no longer feeds hash factors. **0.27.1 affected; 0.29 (dev) appears immune.**

> **Note — candidate explanations for the immunity (testable).** (a) 0.29's `compute_hash` factor set changed, so whatever mutates in the window no longer feeds any hash factor; (b) 0.29's warmup path no longer mutates `VllmConfig` in place; (c) both. One measured datum supports (a): the recorded `cache_key_factors` env-key set grew from **231 keys (0.27.1) to 238 (0.29)** across our two deployments — 26 added feature-flag knobs (new decoder kernels, data/context parallelism, XPU and CPU-offload switches, hardware-agnostic keys, etc.) and 19 removed legacy keys. Pinning the immunity to (a), (b), or (c) requires the field-diff instrumentation outlined below.

## Impact

- The draft compile cache is effectively **startup-history-dependent**: identical configs produce different cache identities depending on whether the main model compiles. Warm-start fleets see surprise recompiles (~196 s per flip; 17 same-signature restarts in one incident window here).
- More generally: **any in-place mutation of `VllmConfig` between the first and last compile of a single startup silently changes derived cache keys** — a reproducibility hazard for torch.compile caching beyond speculative decoding.

## Isolating the field (planned)

Static analysis is exhausted (12+ write points audited). The only leak-free method is instrumenting a real 0.27.1 engine: monkeypatch `VllmConfig.compute_hash` and dump every sub-config's `get_hash_factors()` at backbone vs eagle `__call__`, then field-diff. We plan to run this and will comment with the exact field(s).

> **Note.** Offline worker-derive attempts (calling `VllmConfig.compute_hash` from a separate probe process) produce a `config_hash` different from the in-engine value; all forensic claims in this issue therefore rely exclusively on the on-disk `cache_key_factors.json` snapshots as the source of record.

## Notes

- Authored anonymously by maintainers of two independent production deployments (same as #58653).
- Anonymized forensic snapshots (`cache_key_factors.json` diffs, four-point timeline) available on request.
- Reproduction was performed on 0.27.1 stable; the 0.29 control is a development build — verification on 0.29 stable is pending and will be posted as a comment.
