On main `9f07d023d07f`, 17 of 32 budget-forced ends were corrupted. The same arm on Model Runner V2 was 0 of 32. The cause is in `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder._update_think_state` (`vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py`, added with #34668). While forcing, it advances through the end sequence on the step's draft tokens rather than on accepted tokens, and forces only one position per step. V2 forces every position of the verification window. The fix is in #52677 (`df93fe6c67`), because that PR forces the same end sequence through the same state machine. #### Reproduction One GB10 (sm_121), main `9f07d023d07f` (precompiled wheel `0.30.1rc1.dev20+g9f07d023d`), torch 2.13.0+cu130, driver 580.173.02, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with its MTP head. ``` VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 vllm serve Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \ --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"max_model_len":262144}' \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_end_str":"I have to give the solution based on the reasoning directly now."}' \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-model-len 262144 \ --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --long-prefill-token-threshold 7840 ``` (plus YaRN `hf-overrides`, the `qwen3_coder` tool parser, and `enable_thinking: false` in the default chat template kwargs) Client: `/v1/chat/completions`, `temperature` 0.7, `reasoning_effort` "xhigh", `thinking_token_budget` 256, `max_tokens` 2048. Two prompts that make the model reason at length (write a fixed line 150 or 250 times in its reasoning, then answer "done" or "prime"), 16 requests each at concurrency 16. `reasoning_end_str` is 14 tokens. The budget fired on all 32. | end sequence | reasoning closed | final answer followed | requests | |---|---|---|---| | intact | yes | yes | 14 | | intact | yes | no, the answer re-entered the loop | 1 | | corrupted | yes | yes | 7 | | corrupted | yes | no, the answer re-entered the loop | 5 | | corrupted | no, reasoning ran to `max_tokens` | no | 5 | | **total** | 27 of 32 closed | 21 of 32 answered | 15 intact, **17 corrupted** | "Intact" means the reasoning ends with the phrase exactly once. What the corrupted ones look like: ``` ...I have the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ...I have to give final based on the analysis now. ...I have to give final based on this directly now. ...I need give the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ...I have considered the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ...I have already the solution based on the reasoning directly now. ``` Same host, model, flags, prompts, budget and client: | run | budget fired | intact | corrupted | closed | final answer | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | main `9f07d023d07f`, V1 | 32 | 15 | **17** | 27 | 21 | | main `9f07d023d07f`, V2 (`Using V2 Model Runner` in the log) | 32 | 32 | 0 | 32 | 25 | | #52677 `df93fe6c67`, V1 | 32 | 32 | 0 | 32 | 26 | Fisher two-sided p = 8.2e-7 for corrupted, main V1 against #52677. The #52677 row is that PR's tree on its own wheel (base `f944491db9`), so it differs from main in more than this fix; the V2 row is main itself. The requests without a final answer in the two clean rows closed intact and then repeated the prompt's line in the answer, which is the prompt doing its job. #### Mechanism (main `9f07d023d07f`) When the budget runs out, lines 422-445 force the first end token at one position (`force_index = [remaining_budget]`, `[0]` or `[spec_len]`). On later steps, lines 447-478 walk `spec_token_ids`: a draft equal to the next end token advances `end_count` and its position is left unforced, and only the first non-matching position (or the bonus slot) is forced. At a matching position the target decides on its own logits. If it samples something else, the matching draft is rejected and the target's token is committed, but `end_count` has already moved past it, so the next step forces from a later index: ``` accepted so far END[0..3] drafts [END[4], x, y] -> end_count 3 -> 5; force position 1 := END[5] position 0 not forced; the target samples T instead of END[4]; T is committed next step forcing resumes at END[6]; END[4] and END[5] are never emitted ``` That is the "I have to give final based on ..." shape above: " final" where " the solution" belongs. Two more cases come from the same walk: - when the drafts reach the last end token, `in_end` is cleared before any of them is verified; - when the transition forces the first end token part-way through the window and the draft there matches it, the positions after it go unforced. #### Unit tests `tests/v1/sample/test_thinking_forced_end_spec.py` (in #52677) drives the holder in the order V1 calls it (bonus pass in `Sampler`, target pass in `RejectionSampler`) with greedy verification, CPU only. Against the unfixed code, 5 of its 6 cases fail: | case | unfixed | fixed | |---|---|---| | thinking budget, target rejects a matching draft | FAIL, emits `[40, 41, 42, 77, 200]` for `[40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 200]` | pass | | thinking budget, forcing starts inside the draft window | FAIL, emits `[40, 77, 41, ...]` | pass | | loop break (#52677), target rejects a matching draft | FAIL, same shape | pass | | loop break (#52677), ramp release runs out | FAIL, same shape | pass | | loop break (#52677), drafts reach the last end token | FAIL, the sequence restarts at token 0 | pass | | control, no draft ever matches | pass | pass | #### The fix in #52677 - progress through the end sequence comes from the accepted output; - every position of the verification window, drafts and bonus, is forced to its own end token; - that includes forcing that starts part-way through a window: the budget transition, the loop-break fire, and the ramp release running out. One runtime file, `vllm/v1/sample/thinking_budget_state.py`, plus the test file. Through #52677's loop breaking, which forces the same end sequence when it detects a repeating reasoning loop (same settings except loop breaking on at 128/4/4 with a 256-token floor, `thinking_token_budget` 32768 so only the loop breaker fires, `max_tokens` 4096): | V1 unless stated | host | code | forced ends | corrupted | never closed | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | without the fix, two runs | spark-6 | `351f7b2c5e` | 51 | 23 | 8 | | an earlier version of the fix | spark-6 | on `351f7b2c5e` | 24 | 0 | 0 | | without the fix | spark-5 | `a650585283` | 25 | 6 | 2 | | with the fix | spark-5 | `df93fe6c67` | 25 | 0 | 0 | | with the fix, V2 | spark-5 | `df93fe6c67` | 24 | 0 | 0 | On spark-5 the two V1 rows are one commit apart: 6 of 25 against 0 of 25, Fisher p = 0.022. Matching fires by the scheduler log's request ID instead of by the phrase gives 7 of 26 against 0 of 25 (p = 0.0098), because one unfixed request lost the phrase's tail too. The unfixed rate differs between the hosts (23 of 51 against 6 of 25) at different commits with one or two runs each, so I would not read anything into that gap. #### Limits - V1 only. V2 is the default runner from v0.29.0 (#53183), and main on V2 was clean in the same arm. - One model, one phrase, one GPU type, n = 32 per row. A forced end is corrupted only when the model disagrees with a correct draft inside the end sequence, so the rate depends on the model, the phrase and the temperature. At temperature 0 on the same model, a separate run saw no corruption in 297 such positions. - In spec mode, when a batch has no drafts at all and V1 uses the plain sampler, the holder's row layout gives each request zero rows. That predates this and is not addressed here. #### Related, and why this is not a duplicate - #39697, with open fixes #43210 and #53572: the holder misses a natural reasoning end when `reasoning_end_str` carries a transition phrase, and forces the phrase into the answer. Same file, different defect. Neither diff touches the draft walk at lines 447-478. - #58231: `thinking_token_budget` with speculative decoding and `top_p < 1` emits token id 0 instead of the forced end. Same configuration, different cause (split-row top-p masking in `topk_topp_triton.py`). The corruption here is real vocabulary, never token 0. Searched open and closed issues and PRs for `_update_think_state`, `ThinkingBudgetStateHolder`, `reasoning_end_str`, and "thinking budget" with speculative decoding / MTP / spec decode.

title: [RFC]: Attention Backend Refactor
body:
*Follow-up to [RFC 42082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082) (Standardize KV-cache Layouts). The KV layout standardization can proceed independently (we should complete this first to avoid excessive thrash; this RFC proposes a more aggressive refactor of the attention backend and KV cache manager interfaces.*

### Motivation.

Each attention backend today requires **four interlinked classes** (~750–1000 lines per backend):

| Class | Instances | Role |
|:------|:------------|:-----|
| `AttentionBackend` | (none) static | capability queries, factory methods |
| `AttentionMetadataBuilder` | 1 per group |  builds `AttentionMetadata` each step |
| `AttentionMetadata` | 1 per group per step | backend-specific batch state |
| `AttentionImpl` | 1 per layer | per-layer config; calls kernel in `forward()` |

Problems:
1. **High boilerplate.** Writing a new backend means implementing 4 classes . Adding fields `AttentionMetadata` requires  modifications to `AttentionMetadataBuilder`, `AttentionMetadata` and `AttentionImpl`
2. **Global manager registry.** A hardcoded `spec_manager_map` (679–686 in `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`) decides which manager handles each spec type. Adding a new spec type or a model-specific eviction policy requires patching this shared map plus extending the `is_uniform_type()` isinstance chain.
3. **Coupled concerns in `KVCacheSpec`.** Block allocation policy (how many blocks, when to recycle) and tensor layout (head dims, dtype, page layout) are bundled in one object. Layers that share allocation behavior but differ in tensor layout can't share a block table without the `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` wrapper.



### Proposed Change.

Two independent changes:

#### 1. Single `AttentionBackend` Class

Collapse the four classes into one. The backend manages its own state — no separate metadata type.

```python
class AttentionBackend(ABC):

    def get_cache_config(self) -> tuple[
        type[SingleTypeKVCacheManager],
        ManagerConfig,
        KVCacheTensorSpec,
    ]:
        """Return the manager class, its config, and the tensor spec
        this backend needs. Layers with equal (cls, config) share a
        block table."""
        ...

    def bind_kv_caches(self, kv_caches: dict[str, Tensor],
                       block_table_map: dict[str, int]) -> None:
        """Bind allocated KV cache tensors and block-table mapping.
        block_table_map: layer_name → kv_cache_group_id."""
        ...

    def prep_forward(self, common_attn_metadata: CommonAttentionMetadata,
                     block_tables: dict[int, Tensor],
                     for_cudagraph_capture: bool = False) -> None:
        """Build backend-specific state once per step.
        block_tables: kv_cache_group_id → block table tensor.
        Replaces the MetadataBuilder + Metadata pair."""
        ...

    def forward(self, layer_config: LayerConfig,
                output: Tensor, query: Tensor, key: Tensor,
                value: Tensor, **kwargs) -> Tensor:
        """Execute attention for one layer. Per-layer differences
        (scale, sliding_window, num_heads) come via LayerConfig.
        KV cache is already bound via bind_kv_caches."""
        ...
```

##### Simplified Runner Loop

Today the runner iterates a nested 2D structure (KV cache groups × attention groups) and delegates to a complex `_build_attn_group_metadata` path that handles builder state management, metadata caching, and type translation:

```python
# Current (~1289–1401 in gpu_model_runner.py): nested loop
for kv_cache_group_id, kv_cache_group_spec in enumerate(...):
    # ... build CommonAttentionMetadata ...
    for attn_group in self.attn_groups[kv_cache_group_id]:
        builder = attn_group.get_metadata_builder()
        attn_metadata_i = builder.build(
            common_prefix_len=...,
            common_attn_metadata=common_attn_metadata,
        )
        for layer_name in attn_group.layer_names:
            attn_metadata[layer_name] = attn_metadata_i
```

With backends managing their own state via `prep_forward`, the runner flattens to a single loop over attention groups. Each group can span multiple KV cache groups — relevant block tables are passed as a dict:

```python
# Proposed: flat loop
for attn_group in self.attn_groups:
    attn_group.backend.prep_forward(
        common_metadata,
        block_tables={gid: block_tables[gid]
                      for gid in attn_group.kv_cache_group_ids},
    )
```

The metadata builder abstraction, metadata caching layer, and the `attn_metadata` dict that maps layer names to per-step metadata objects all go away.

##### Migration

A `LegacyBackendAdapter` wraps existing 4-class backends, forwarding `prep_forward` → builder + build and `forward` → impl.forward. Backends migrate incrementally.

#### 2. Backends Declare Manager + Tensor Spec

Today `KVCacheSpec` conflates block allocation and tensor layout. Because they're bundled, the `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` wrapper exists solely to group layers with matching allocation policy but different page sizes — and `is_uniform_type()` must be extended with a new isinstance branch for every new spec type.

Instead, **each backend returns the manager it needs**:

```python
(manager_cls, manager_config, kv_cache_tensor_spec)
```

- **`manager_cls` + `manager_config`** — block allocation policy. Layers with equal `(manager_cls, manager_config)` share a block table. This replaces `spec_manager_map`, `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`, and `is_uniform_type()`.
- **`kv_cache_tensor_spec`** — physical tensor layout (the `KVCacheTensorSpec` from [RFC 42082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082)). Stays on the worker, never crosses to the scheduler.

##### Manager Configs

Each manager defines a frozen `Config` dataclass carrying only allocation-policy fields. `block_size` and `num_blocks` are constructor parameters (global values determined by the worker), not part of the config.

```python
class FullAttentionManager(SingleTypeKVCacheManager):
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Config:
        pass

class SlidingWindowManager(SingleTypeKVCacheManager):
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Config:
        sliding_window: int

class MambaManager(SingleTypeKVCacheManager):
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class Config:
        mamba_cache_mode: str
        num_speculative_blocks: int
```

Models can supply custom managers (e.g. a model-specific eviction policy) by returning a different `manager_cls` from `get_cache_config()` — no patching of shared registries.

##### Worker-Driven Allocation

The worker has the model, the backends, and the GPU. It owns grouping and tensor allocation — the engine only needs allocation policy and a block budget:

```
Worker:           collect (manager_cls, manager_config, tensor_spec) per backend
Worker:           group by (manager_cls, manager_config) equality
Worker:           compute block_size, kernel_block_size, num_blocks
Worker → Engine:  SchedulerKVCacheConfig { num_blocks, block_size, groups }
Engine:           min(num_blocks) across workers → broadcast agreed value
Worker:           allocate tensors locally with agreed num_blocks
```

The scheduler never sees `KVCacheTensorSpec`. Tensor layout plans no longer cross the process boundary.

### What Disappears

| Today | After |
|:------|:------|
| `spec_manager_map` (global dict) | Gone — `manager_cls` returned by backend |
| `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` + `is_uniform_type()` isinstance chain | Gone — `(cls, config)` equality |
| `KVCacheTensor` layout plan crossing to engine | Gone — worker allocates locally |
| 4-class backend structure (Backend + Builder + Metadata + Impl) | Gone — single `AttentionBackend` |
| `get_kv_cache_shape()` / `get_kv_cache_stride_order()` on backend | Gone — lives on `KVCacheTensorSpec` ([RFC 42082](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082)) |
| Per-layer `AttentionImpl` instances | Gone — Layer specifics passed to `forward()` |

### Trade-offs

- **Model definitions must manage backend sharing.** Today the runner creates one `AttentionImpl` per layer automatically. With the unified backend, the model is responsible for ensuring layers that should share a backend actually reference the same instance. This is more explicit but slightly more work for model authors.
- **`LegacyBackendAdapter` is needed during migration.** All existing backends continue working behind the adapter, but the adapter adds one indirection layer until each backend is ported natively.



### Feedback Period.

_No response_

### CC List.

@MatthewBonanni @WoosukKwon @heheda12345 

### Worktracking

TODO: start work following https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42082
TODO: develop follow-up RFC for plugins @MatthewBonanni

title: [Bug] MiMoV2 load_weights: fused qkv_proj path uses naive chunk(tp,dim=0)[rank], misplaces Q values into K/V slots
body:
## Summary

`vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py:load_weights` has a code path for fused-`qkv_proj` checkpoints (MiMo-V2 Pro variants) that does

```python
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    if name in params_dict:
        param = params_dict[name]
        loaded_weight = loaded_weight.chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]
        default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
    continue
```

For a checkpoint where the fused tensor is laid out `[Q | K | V]` along dim 0 — which is the case for at least `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` — a naive `chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]` gives 7 of 8 ranks (at TP=8) rows that fall entirely inside the Q region. Those ranks' `QKVParallelLinear` parameter slots for K and V end up filled with Q values; only the last rank gets any real K/V data. Attention is therefore severely broken on 7 of 8 ranks.

The proper loader (`QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader` with `shard_id="q"/"k"/"v"`) handles the TP split per-section correctly. It's already used by the `stacked_params_mapping` path for checkpoints that store Q/K/V as separate tensors; the fused path just doesn't reach it.

## Repro

Model: `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` (the only Pro-format quant I'm aware of that hits the fused branch; the Flash variant stores split q_proj/k_proj/v_proj and goes through `stacked_params_mapping`, which is correct).

Cluster: 8-node DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=8, Ray distributed executor. With other patches in place (MXFP8 dispatch wired into `modelopt_mixed`, `weight_scale_inv` -> `weight_scale` rename for the modelopt MXFP8 scale parameter), the model reaches Application startup and serves requests, but inference returns degenerate token loops (`*\0` / `Müslü` / `the` style — varies with prompt but never coherent).

## Empirical evidence the layout is `Q→K→V` (not per-rank pre-sharded)

For layer 0 `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight_scale_inv` (shape `[27136, 192]`, uint8 E8M0):

| Region (dim-0 slice) | Rows | Mean byte | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q section `[0:24576]` | 24576 | **114.55** | 24576 = 128 Q heads × 192 head_dim |
| K section `[24576:26112]` | 1536 | **115.99** | 1536 = 8 KV heads × 192 head_dim |
| V section `[26112:27136]` | 1024 | **113.27** | 1024 = 8 KV heads × 128 v_head_dim |

The three sections have distinguishable scale-byte distributions (note V is systematically smaller-magnitude, consistent with `attention_value_scale=0.612` applied to V before attention). If the tensor were per-rank pre-sharded (8 chunks of `[Q|K|V]` concatenated), every chunk would have the same internal structure and the per-rank means would be identical; instead they're flat ~114 for the first 7 chunks (all-Q) and a weighted mix for chunk 7 (which spans the Q/K/V boundaries).

## Fix

Split the fused tensor by `(q_size, k_size, v_size)` using config dims (distinguishing full vs. SWA layers via `hybrid_layer_pattern`), then call the existing `QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader` three times with `shard_id` `"q"`, `"k"`, `"v"`. Each call lets the proper loader take this rank's TP-slice of that section, identical to the existing stacked path.

Proposed patch against `vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py` (replacing the `if "qkv_proj" in name:` block):

```python
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    if name in params_dict:
        param = params_dict[name]
        try:
            _li = int(name.split(".layers.")[1].split(".")[0])
        except (IndexError, ValueError):
            _li = -1
        _is_swa = (
            _li >= 0
            and hasattr(self.config, "hybrid_layer_pattern")
            and self.config.hybrid_layer_pattern[_li] == 1
        )
        if _is_swa:
            _nh = self.config.swa_num_attention_heads
            _nkv = self.config.swa_num_key_value_heads
            _hd = self.config.swa_head_dim
            _vhd = getattr(self.config, "swa_v_head_dim", _hd)
        else:
            _nh = self.config.num_attention_heads
            _nkv = self.config.num_key_value_heads
            _hd = self.config.head_dim
            _vhd = getattr(self.config, "v_head_dim", _hd)
        _qs = _nh * _hd
        _ks = _nkv * _hd
        _vs = _nkv * _vhd
        if loaded_weight.shape[0] == _qs + _ks + _vs:
            _q = loaded_weight[:_qs]
            _k = loaded_weight[_qs : _qs + _ks]
            _v = loaded_weight[_qs + _ks : _qs + _ks + _vs]
            _wl = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
            _wl(param, _q, "q")
            _wl(param, _k, "k")
            _wl(param, _v, "v")
            loaded_params.add(name)
        else:
            # Unexpected shape — keep old behavior.
            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]
            default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
    continue
```

I have this running on a TP=8 cluster; with the patch, the same model produces coherent output for chat and completion prompts (`12 × 7` → `84`, `def fibonacci(n):` → proper Python recursion, etc.). Without the patch, the same configuration produces the degenerate token loops described above.

The patch handles both full and SWA layers (MiMo-V2 has full attention layers at positions where `hybrid_layer_pattern[layer] == 0` and SWA layers elsewhere). It applies to both the FP8 weight tensor and the uint8 E8M0 scale tensor (`weight_scale_inv`) because both share the `qkv_proj` name prefix.

## Why this also affects users who don't see the symptom

The Flash-format MiMo-V2 checkpoints (separate `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`) go through the `stacked_params_mapping` path before hitting this branch, so they're fine. Only fused-`qkv_proj` Pro checkpoints reach the buggy path. To my knowledge today that's `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` and the BF16 source `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-Pro` (if anyone tries to serve it directly).

## Related

- vllm#41797 (DiffKV Triton attention for MiMo) — gets the model past the attention-backend selection blocker; the load-path bug is independent.
- NVIDIA/cutlass#3096, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2776 — the wider sm_121/NVFP4 conversation. For this specific checkpoint the garbage signature `あるい/Müslü` was *not* a CUTLASS Sm120 ArchTag symptom; the same garbage class shows up across MXFP8 attention kernels (Marlin / Emulation / FlashInferCutlass) and NVFP4 MoE backends (Marlin / CUTLASS / Emulation) — only the load-side fix above clears it.

Happy to open a PR with the patch + a small test. Wanted to file the diagnosis first so the analysis isn't buried.

Working repo with patches + recipe: https://github.com/idonati/spark-vllm-docker-festr2

title: [Hybrid SSM] Investigate accuracy divergence between `mamba_chunk_scan` and `selective_state_update` kernels
body:
## Context

PR #43186 lowered the gsm8k accuracy threshold for `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` under NIXL PD disagg after #42430 rerouted the D-side 1-token recompute from `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` to `selective_state_update` (SSU).

The two kernels produce different bf16 outputs due (supposedly) different reduction orders:
- `mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` goes through bf16 matmul with intermediate bf16 casts (`tl.dot`)
- `selective_state_update` keeps the SSM step in fp32 throughout

As noted in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43186#issuecomment-2893988543), this seems like a large accuracy drop for something meant to be algebraically equivalent.

## Goal

Investigate the kernel-level numerical divergence **in isolation** to:
1. **Quantify the magnitude**: Run both kernels on identical inputs for a single prompt (prefill + decode) and measure the output divergence (max abs diff, relative error distribution).
2. **Determine hardware dependence**: Test on at least **Ampere (A100)** and **Hopper (H100)** to see if the divergence magnitude or direction is architecture-dependent.
3. **Recommend a fix or acceptable tolerance**: Based on findings, either align the kernels' numeric behavior or document the expected tolerance.

## Reproduction Plan

- Isolate the two kernels (`mamba_chunk_scan_combined_varlen` and `selective_state_update`) with a single-prompt workload (1 prefill + N decode steps).
- Compare outputs element-wise against each other and against an fp64 reference.
- Run on Ampere (A100) and Hopper (H100) hardware.

## References

- PR that lowered threshold: #43186
- PR that rerouted to SSU: #42430

title: [Bug]: test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion fails with FlashAttnMLA + fp8 KV cache (NotImplementedError)
body:
### Your current environment

- vllm `0.23.0` (PyPI release) and `vllm-project/vllm@main` (also reproduced on a downstream fork at the same upstream sha)
- transformers: verified on both `4.57.1` and `5.12.1` (latest stable, released 2026-06-15) — same failure
- 1 × NVIDIA H20, CUDA 13.0, torch `2.11.0+cu130`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py::test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion` parametrizes over `kv_cache_dtype=["auto", "fp8"]` × `MLA_BACKENDS = [TRITON_MLA, FLASH_ATTN_MLA, ROCM_AITER_MLA]`. On Hopper (where `flash_attn_supports_mla()` is True) two combinations are collected and both fail at backend construction:

```
test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion[fp8-dtype0-True-16-512-1536-128-64-128-16-True-AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN_MLA]
test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion[fp8-dtype0-False-16-512-1536-128-64-128-16-True-AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN_MLA]
```

Stack:
```
E   NotImplementedError: FlashAttnMLA V1 with FP8 KV cache not yet supported
```

raised by `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py` when constructing the backend.

### Reproducer

```bash
pytest -v tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py \
       -k "FLASH_ATTN_MLA and fp8"
```

Expected: 2 collected, both either pass or be cleanly skipped.
Actual: 2 failed (after pytest-rerunfailures retries them).

### Where it came from

`tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py` was added in #40392 (merged 2026-05-11) and has not been touched since (only one commit on the file). The parametrize matrix unconditionally crosses `kv_cache_dtype=["auto", "fp8"]` with all `MLA_BACKENDS`. There is no `skipif` for the `(FLASH_ATTN_MLA, fp8)` cell, even though `FlashAttnMLA` explicitly raises `NotImplementedError` for FP8 KV cache.

### Suggested options (no preference, just listing)

1. Implement FP8 KV cache support in `FlashAttnMLA` so the parametrize matrix can stand.
2. Add a `pytest.skip(...)` runtime check in `test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion` for `(attn_backend == FLASH_ATTN_MLA and kv_cache_dtype == "fp8")`, mirroring the `flashattn_mla.py` capability gate.
3. Filter `MLA_BACKENDS` to drop `FLASH_ATTN_MLA` when `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8"` at test collection time.

Filing this only as a report — happy to put up a PR for any of the three if a maintainer indicates the preferred direction.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Bug]: No clamp-capable batched NVFP4 fused-MoE backend → DeepEP / wide-EP unusable for MiniMax-M3 NVFP4
body:
### Environment

vLLM mainline with the NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 MoE path (the standard `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m3`
build + the NVFP4 MoE support from PR #46380), on Blackwell sm_100, NVLink-only (no InfiniBand),
with `deep_ep` and `nvshmem` available.

### What's wrong

NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 serves fine with normal expert parallelism. But the moment you turn on
**DeepEP** for wide-EP on the decode workers (e.g. `data-parallel-size: 16` +
`all2all-backend: deepep_low_latency`), it dies at startup:

```
NotImplementedError: No NvFp4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration.
  (vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py, select_nvfp4_moe_backend)
```

DeepEP itself comes up fine first — you can see `Using DeepEPLLAll2AllManager` and the EP rank
map being built — so this isn't a DeepEP or NVSHMEM problem. It's that none of the NVFP4 MoE
kernels can handle DeepEP's batched layout **and** MiniMax-M3's SwiGLU clamp at the same time.

### Why it happens

MiniMax-M3's experts use SwiGLU-OAI with a clamp (`swiglu_limit`). Two requirements collide:

- **The clamp** is only implemented by one NVFP4 backend, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM`. When
  `swiglu_limit` is set, the backend picker (`NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`) narrows the choices
  down to TRTLLM only.
- **DeepEP** needs the *batched* activation format, and the only NVFP4 backend that provides it,
  `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED`, does SILU only — no SwiGLU, no clamp.

So "I need the clamp" forces TRTLLM (which is standard-layout only), and "I need DeepEP" forces
the batched kernel (which has no clamp). No single backend does both:

| backend | applies SwiGLU clamp? | supports batched (DeepEP) layout? | activations |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` | ✅ (the only one) | ❌ standard only | SILU, RELU2, GELU(_TANH), SWIGLUOAI, SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE |
| `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED` | ❌ | ✅ (the only one) | SILU only |
| `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` | ❌ | ❌ | SILU, GELU_TANH, RELU2, SWIGLUOAI |

Forcing the batched backend by hand doesn't get around it either — you just hit a guard:
`ValueError: Model sets swiglu_limit=..., but the requested moe_backend does not apply the SwiGLU clamp.`

### A separate snag on NVLink-only systems

If you reach for `deepep_high_throughput` instead, it fails even earlier, while DeepEP is
setting up its buffers:

```
deep_ep/buffer.py ... RuntimeError: CUDA error 'invalid resource handle'
```

High-throughput mode expects InfiniBand RDMA between nodes. On NVLink-only multi-node systems
there's no IB, so it can't start. `deepep_low_latency` + `VLLM_DEEPEP_LOW_LATENCY_USE_MNNVL=1`
is the right transport there, and it *does* start — it just then runs into the backend gap above.

### How to tell it's activation-specific, not a clamp bug

A SiLU-activated NVFP4 MoE (`hidden_act="silu"` + clamp) works fine, because SILU is supported by
both TRTLLM (clamp, standard layout) and CUTEDSL_BATCHED. The gap is specifically the
**SwiGLU-OAI + clamp** combination on a **batched** NVFP4 kernel.

### What would fix it

Teach a *batched* NVFP4 MoE backend to do SwiGLU-OAI (uninterleaved) with the clamp, and add it
to `NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP`. Two plausible routes:

1. Add a **masked**-layout version of the cute-DSL swiglu-fusion kernel that already exists for
   the contiguous layout (`flashinfer/.../blockscaled_contiguous_gather_grouped_gemm_swiglu_fusion`).
   The DeepEP/batched path uses the masked grouped GEMM, which currently has no swiglu fusion.
2. Or add a `swigluoai_clamp_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize` op (like the existing SILU-only
   `silu_and_mul_scaled_nvfp4_experts_quantize`) and wire it into `FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_BATCHED`.

This is basically the batched counterpart of #45624, which added the same activation + clamp to
the standard-layout TRTLLM backend. Until something like it lands, NVFP4 MiniMax-M3 is limited to
standard EP and can't use DeepEP wide-EP.

title: [Bug]: /v1/realtime audio sessions can retain KV cache indefinitely when clients stay connected without final=True
body:
### Your current environment

## Environment

- vLLM V1
- `/v1/realtime`
- Realtime audio transcription, e.g. Voxtral realtime models

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

In the `/v1/realtime` audio WebSocket API, a client can keep a realtime session alive indefinitely by leaving the WebSocket connection open and never sending `input_audio_buffer.commit` with `final: true`.

For V1 realtime streaming requests, normal non-final commits keep the request resumable and extend the session context. KV blocks are only released when the request is actually finalized, aborted, or the WebSocket connection is closed. If the client remains connected but stops sending audio/final, the server has no application-layer idle timeout to force cleanup.

## Impact

This can cause KV cache usage to grow or remain pinned for stale realtime sessions. In production, stale clients can eventually push KV cache usage to 100%, requiring manual intervention such as closing client connections or restarting pods.

## Current Behavior

A realtime audio session is cleaned up when:

- The client sends `input_audio_buffer.commit` with `final: true`
- The WebSocket disconnects
- The server detects the connection is gone and cleanup runs

However, if the WebSocket stays open and the client stops sending valid audio or never sends `final: true`, the realtime session can continue occupying engine-side resources.

Repeated non-final commits also do not represent actual new audio input, but they can keep the application-level session alive.

## Expected Behavior

Realtime audio WebSocket sessions should have a server-side idle policy. If no valid audio input is received for a configurable timeout, the server should gracefully finalize or close the session so the underlying engine request can unwind and release KV cache.

## Proposed Fix

Add an application-layer idle watchdog to `RealtimeConnection`:

- Default timeout: 30 seconds
- Configurable via an environment variable
- Reset the watchdog on valid `input_audio_buffer.append`
- Reset on non-final `commit` only when it actually starts generation
- Do not let repeated no-op commits keep the session alive
- On timeout, enqueue the final audio sentinel to gracefully finish the streaming request
- If graceful finalization does not complete within a short grace period, cancel the generation task and close the WebSocket

This gives operators a practical safety valve for stale realtime clients while preserving explicit `final=True` behavior for well-behaved clients.

title: [Bug] TPU: State leak in FP8 MoE shared_experts after AOT compilation fails with prefix caching
body:
### Your current environment

1. Environment: TPU v6e-8
2. Image: `vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260626-c539adc-cc79815`


### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Description
When running an FP8 MoE model (`Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`) on TPU v6e with `--enable-prefix-caching` enabled, the engine crashes during the warmup phase with an `AssertionError` in `shared_experts.py`. 

The root cause appears to be a state leak in the FP8 `shared_experts` module triggered by a failed AOT compilation attempt. 

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Environment: TPU v6e-8
2. Image: `vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260626-c539adc-cc79815`
3. Command:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --trust-remote-code
```  

### Relevant Log Output
```(EngineCore pid=602) INFO 06-26 17:58:38 [compilation_manager.py:133] Precompile worker0 backbone --> {'num_tokens': 2048, 'num_reqs': 64}
(EngineCore pid=602) INFO 06-26 17:58:39 [compilation_manager.py:156] AOT lower skipped for worker0 backbone (ValueError('Invalid shape for `swap`... ')); will compile in warmup.
...
(EngineCore pid=602) ERROR 06-26 17:58:42 [core.py:1231]   File "/workspace/vllm/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/shared_experts.py", line 165, in forward
(EngineCore pid=602) ERROR 06-26 17:58:42 [core.py:1231]     assert self._output[self._output_idx] is None
(EngineCore pid=602) ERROR 06-26 17:58:42 [core.py:1231] AssertionError
``` 

### Root Cause Analysis
1.) The engine attempts AOT compilation for various input shapes. It succeeds up to num_tokens=1024.
2.) When attempting to compile num_tokens=2048, AOT lowering fails due to a shape mismatch in the prefix caching swap logic:
```AOT lower skipped for worker0 backbone (ValueError('Invalid shape for swap. Ref shape: (2, 0, 2048). Expected shape: (0, 32). Value shape: (1, 32)... ')); will compile in warmup.```

3.) The State Leak: The FP8 shared_experts module does not clear its internal state after this aborted AOT pass.

4.) When the engine immediately moves to the warmup phase and attempts to trace the model, it hits the uncleared state and crashes here:
assert self._output[self._output_idx] is None -> AssertionError

### Additional Context
1.) This bug is a regression. The identical configuration runs successfully on an older image (vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260612-c0c56aa-8a91228).

2.) The crash requires the combination of FP8 MoE (requantizing to float8_e4m3fn), AOT compilation, and --enable-prefix-caching.

title: [Bug][Metrics] `get_metrics_snapshot()` raises on unknown metric types, crashing LLM.get_metrics() and the ORCA header path
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`vllm/v1/metrics/reader.py::get_metrics_snapshot()` dispatches over
`metric.type` for every `vllm:`-prefixed entry in
`prometheus_client.REGISTRY`, but its dispatch is closed over
`{gauge, counter, histogram}`. The trailing `else` branch raises:

```python
else:
    raise AssertionError(f"Unknown metric type {metric.type}")
```

(`vllm/v1/metrics/reader.py:141` on current `main`.)

### Impact

`prometheus_client` ships `Summary`, `Info`, `Stateset`, and `untyped`
as first-class metric types, and OTel's `gen_ai.server.request.duration`
semantic convention is conventionally exported as `Summary`. The day
anyone adds a `Summary`-typed metric (or any custom collector that
returns `metric.type == \"untyped\"`) prefixed `vllm:`, two live code
paths crash:

1. **`vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py:380` → public `LLM.get_metrics()`**
   offline library API. Every offline caller reading in-memory metrics
   would crash.
2. **`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/orca_metrics.py:90` → `metrics_header()`**
   on `/v1/chat/completions` requests that opt into the
   `endpoint-load-metrics` ORCA header. Every such requests returns
   HTTP 500.

### Root cause

The available prometheus_client family of metric types is wider than
the three the reader handles, and the trailing branch fails loudly
instead of degrading gracefully.

### Suggested fix

Replace the `raise AssertionError(...)` with a graceful
`logger.debug(\"Skipping unknown metric type %s for metric %s\", ...)`
+ `continue`, matching the existing unknown-type handling pattern
already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g.
`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/metrics.py:189`,
`:216`, `:451`).

### Relationship to existing work

- [PR #35649](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35649)
  \"Replace bare AssertionError with specific exception types\" touches
  the same line and proposes `raise ValueError(...)`. That keeps the
  production hazard: the reader still crashes both live consumers; it
  just does so with a different exception class. The behaviour this
  issue proposes (skip, not raise) is materially different: it
  prioritises availability for the library/header consumers, which were
  never in a position to read a metric type they have no dataclass for
  anyway.

### Environment

Found while auditing the V1 metrics subsystem on `main` at
`867fd5e8ed6b0bfcf84b24f82658c9fb698a6d35` (2026-06-27). The bug is
not environment-specific: it reproduces whenever any future
`vllm:`-prefixed metric uses a type outside `{gauge, counter, histogram}`.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I searched for relevant existing issues (no existing report
  found for the crash; #35649 is a related refactor with a materially
  different behaviour proposal).

---
*The fix and analysis above were investigated with AI assistance
(Claude); the underlying source locations and reasoning were reviewed
by me before filing.*

title: [Bug][ROCm]: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 cannot load on ROCm, the AMD Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding has no FP8 weight_scale
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM v0.30.0, image `docker.io/vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:v0.30.0` (amd64 `sha256:2e7da1ad1c66836802072588adea75f9f4991da5f9545b4318e91d422c22ce6a`) with fastokens 0.3.1 added, nothing else changed
- 8x AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), ROCm driver 6.19.14
- Kubernetes, TP 4 on four of the eight cards
- The same failure on v0.29.0


### 🐛 Describe the bug

`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` at revision `236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13` fails in weight loading on ROCm. Every worker dies with the same error:

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'ngram_embedding.weight_scale' in Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding. The available parameters belonging to ngram_embedding (PLEVocabParallelEmbedding) are: {'ngram_embedding.weight'}
```

Command, run inside the image:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 \
  --revision 236dfdf285828023ca3bcd3f37366c58a3469b13 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85
```

The checkpoint is `quant_method: fp8` with `weight_block_size: [128, 128]` and dynamic activations. Its n-gram embedding table is F8_E4M3 with one BF16 global scale stored as `ngram_embedding.weight_scale`.

**Why it still fails after #54722 and #54882.** Both PRs are in v0.30.0, and both fix the FP8 PLE scale in the NVIDIA model path only (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/`). The ROCm build takes `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/amd/ple_layer.py`, which defines its own `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding` with no FP8 method and no `weight_scale` parameter. The scale tensor has nowhere to land on AMD. This is still true on main after #57497. #54765 is the NVIDIA report of the same error.

**What works.** `--enable-expert-parallel` gets the checkpoint past the block-quant check that stops plain TP 4 and TP 8 (expert width 640 against a 128 block gives 160 or 80 per rank). With EP the workers reach weight loading and fail only on the scale above. The bf16 checkpoint `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` serves on the same box and image.

**Ask.** Port the FP8 PLE weight-scale handling into the AMD `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding`, or share one embedding method between the two paths. Until then the FP8 checkpoint cannot be served on ROCm at any TP, on MI325X or MI355X.

I can test a fix on MI325X.

title: [Bug]: MTP fails to load dense BF16 MTP head on compressed-tensors pack-quantized checkpoints (no module or parameter named 'fc.weight')
body:
## Bug Description

`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp",...}'` crashes at weight-load time when the target checkpoint is **compressed-tensors pack-quantized** and ships its MTP head as **dense BF16** in a separate shard. The MTP predictor's Linear layers are built from the *target's* quant config, so the loader expects packed parameter names (`weight_packed`) while the checkpoint provides dense `mtp.*.weight` tensors.

## Environment

- vLLM v0.30.0, official docker image `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` (stock, no patches)
- Model: [`ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-W4A16-AWQ`](https://huggingface.co/ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-W4A16-AWQ) (dense 27B, `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, hybrid GDN + full attention, vision preserved)
- Flags: `vllm serve ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27b-W4A16-AWQ --tensor-parallel-size 2 --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'` (+ kv fp8; the crash is at load, the rest is irrelevant)

## Crash

```
ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight' in Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor
```

Raised from the weight-map walk in `vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py` (`_load_module`, the "no module or parameter named" branch), reached via `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.load_weights` (`vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`). The engine never reaches runtime — deterministic at boot.

## Root Cause

`Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor.__init__` builds its `fc` (`ColumnParallelLinear`) and decoder layers from `vllm_config.quant_config` — the **target's** config. The file already contains two workarounds for the dense-draft-on-quantized-target family:

1. `modelopt_fp4`: `fc_quant = None` because "mtp.fc is stored as BF16 in NVFP4 checkpoints but is missing from hf_quant_config.json exclude_modules" (PR #38650)
2. GPTQ: `quantization_config.dynamic` `-:mtp` patterns → build all MTP layers unquantized

**Neither covers compressed-tensors.** For this checkpoint:

- `config.json` → `quantization_config.format: "pack-quantized"`, method `compressed-tensors`; the `ignore` list covers `model.visual.*`, `model.language_model.layers.*.linear_attn*`, `lm_head` — **no `mtp` entry**
- `model.safetensors.index.json` → 15 `mtp.*` tensors, **all dense** (plain `.weight` names, e.g. `mtp.fc.weight`, `mtp.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight`), all in a dedicated `model-mtp-bf16.safetensors` shard

So the quantizer left the MTP head unquantized **without declaring it in `ignore`**, vLLM builds the MTP Linears pack-quantized, and the dense names cannot resolve.

This is a cousin of #51581 (DFlash2 `_build_context_kv_buffers` slicing `.weight` on a pack-quantized target) — same family of draft/MTP structures assuming dense parameters on quantized targets.

## Suggested Fix

Extend the existing workaround family: when the target quant config is compressed-tensors (pack-quantized) and the checkpoint's MTP tensors are dense — detectable either from the safetensors index (plain `mtp.*.weight` names, no packed variants) or from a dedicated bf16 MTP shard — build the MTP predictor unquantized, mirroring the `modelopt_fp4` path for `fc` and the GPTQ `dynamic` path for the layers.

Happy to provide the full boot log or test a fix branch — the checkpoint and repro are on hand.

title: [Feature]: [ROCm][AITER][Hy4] Enable gfx950 MXFP8 MoE and dense linear backends
body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

`tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8` runs on gfx950 through the ROCm support added in #57526, but its ModelOpt MXFP8 operations currently use Triton even when `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`:
```text
Using RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
Using 'TRITON_MXFP8' MxFp8 MoE backend.
```
This feature request tracks two independent AITER enablement categories. 

cc: @akii96 (I know you're focused on gfx942, but wanted to keep you in the loop)

### 1. MXFP8 MoE enablement
vLLM already provides `AiterMxfp8Experts`, but its compatibility check rejects Hy4.
The current AITER implementation requires:
- `SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE`
- SwiGLU alpha `1.702`
- SwiGLU beta `1.0`
Hy4 instead uses clamped SwiGLU:
```text
gate = clamp(gate, max=limit)
up   = clamp(up, -limit, limit)
out  = silu(gate) * up
```
The published checkpoint sets `swiglu_limit=10.0`.

#### AITER work
- Support Hy4’s gate/up layout and clamped SwiGLU semantics in the gfx950 MXFP8 fused-MoE kernel.
- Preserve native 1×32 E8M0 weights/scales.
- Support Hy4 routing, expert masks and tensor-parallel execution.
- Add correctness tests against a BF16/dequantized reference.

#### vLLM work
- Represent Hy4’s activation semantics accurately in `FusedMoEConfig`.
- Update `AiterMxfp8Experts.is_supported_config`.
- Forward activation, clamp and gate-layout arguments to AITER.
- Verify automatic selection and explicit `--moe-backend aiter`.
- Preserve `TRITON_MXFP8` fallback.
- Add Hy4 MXFP8 MoE unit and end-to-end coverage.

### 2. MXFP8 dense linear/GEMM enablement
Hy4’s dense projections use ModelOpt MXFP8:
- E4M3 values
- E8M0 scales
- 1×32 scaling blocks
- BF16 output
This is not format-compatible with AITER’s conventional FP8 128×128 block-scale GEMMs. vLLM therefore selects `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`.

#### AITER work
- Add a gfx950 dense MXFP8 GEMM accepting the 1×32 E8M0 format.
- Support dynamic `M`, weight pre-shuffling, split-K and caller-owned output buffers.
- Add runtime configuration lookup, shape logging and a gfx950 tuner.
- Add correctness tests against dequantized BF16.

#### vLLM work
- Add an AITER-backed `Mxfp8LinearKernel`.
- Register it in `_POSSIBLE_MXFP8_KERNELS[PlatformEnum.ROCM]` ahead of Triton when supported.
- Implement gfx950, AITER and scale-layout capability checks.
- Add weight/scale preprocessing and pre-shuffling.
- Support `torch.compile` and full/piecewise cudagraph capture.
- Preserve Triton and emulation fallbacks.
- Add kernel-selection and end-to-end tests.


### Alternatives

- Continue using `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` and `TRITON_MXFP8`.
- Dequantize MXFP8 weights to BF16, with additional memory and performance cost.
- Generic AITER A8W8 block-scale kernels are not a valid substitute because their scale format differs from ModelOpt MXFP8.

title: [Spec Decode][dflash] Drafter KV group is never identified, so prefix-cache reuse is silently disabled for the Mamba groups
body:
AI-authored (disclosed): produced and verified on our live CMP 170HX cluster; the account owner is a user, not a vLLM dev.

### Summary

With `method="dflash"` the drafter's KV cache group is never identified, so the consumer falls back to treating **every** group as a draft group -- including the Mamba/GDN groups -- and prefix-cache reuse across requests is silently disabled for those layers. The warning is printed on every start:

```
Speculative decoding (method=dflash) is enabled but no KV cache group could be
identified as the draft model's, so every group -- including Mamba groups [0, 1, 2, 3]
-- will be treated as a draft group. A Mamba group cannot satisfy the widened lookup
window that implies, so prefix-cache reuse across requests will be disabled ...
```

`_uses_trailing_mtp_layers()` (the positional fallback generalized in #55390) is gated on `spec_config.method == "mtp"`. `dflash` drafts reuse the target's decoder-layer architecture, so their attention spec is indistinguishable from the target's and the spec-driven rule cannot find them either.

### Measured consequence -- corrected

**Correction (2026-09-16, see the validation comment below):** this section originally attributed the
36.4 s prefix-child TTFT to the missing draft-group annotation. That attribution is wrong. With the
annotation patch applied (`xiaoba17/vllm@40681e0c9d`) the same 35-36 s reproduces and the engine's
prefix-cache counters are byte-identical; the annotation fix is correct and worth carrying, but it does
not gate this symptom.

What does gate it is the **Mamba checkpoint retention policy** plus prefill chunk granularity. On the
same box, same payload: `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 832` takes the 51.8k prefix child from
35.15 s to 5.83 s (+74,880 reused tokens = 10 x 7,488), and `--max-num-batched-tokens 1664` takes it to
1.47 s (= an exact re-send) for ~13 % extra on the cold parent prefill. The default
`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0` keeps only semantic replay boundaries, so a child that extends a
cached parent resumes from a much earlier checkpoint. For reference, an **identical** re-send resumes
in 1.5 s in every configuration -- which is why the original comparison looked like an annotation
problem.

### Ask

Extend the trailing-layer positional fallback (with the `_groups_partition_layers_exactly` guard added in #55390) to `method == "dflash"`, or state why it cannot apply there. If dflash drafts are guaranteed to register their KV layers after every target layer the same way MTP drafts do, the rule should transfer; if they are not, some other annotation path is needed, because the flag-all fallback quietly costs the Mamba-group reuse in any dflash deployment.

### Environment / evidence

- vLLM v0.13.0 line (fork image `vllm/vllm-backport:cmp170hx`, sha256 `2d27fe8655b0c57b953dc3dff72034df0a98abf2a1ff07387e48f6a0af886a2a`), V2 GPU model runner.
- Reproducible on every start; no special flags beyond the ones above. Raw server logs, per-request TTFT/JSONL and the harness are kept on the machine and available on request.

---
AI-authored contribution (omp agent). The account owner is a user running these models in production: they reported the failure, asked for the fix, and run it live today. They are not a vLLM developer and do not vouch for the code -- please verify it independently (logs, configs and image digests on request). Thanks for the maintainer work, and apologies for the review load that AI-written reports add; if you would rather not get them, say so and we will stop. If our fix causes trouble, we will keep driving it.
